sentences.zh: 羅憲

translations.literal: Luo Xian — biography heading.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Xian.

sentences.zh: 羅憲，字令則，襄陽人也。

translations.literal: Luo Xian, courtesy name Lingze, was a native of Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Xian, whose courtesy name was Lingze, came from Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 父蒙，蜀廣漢太守。

translations.literal: His father Meng was Administrator of Guanghan in Shu.
translations.idiomatic: His father, Luo Meng, had served as Administrator of Guanghan in Shu.

sentences.zh: 憲年十三，能屬文，早知名。

translations.literal: At thirteen Xian could compose essays and was early known by reputation.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen he could already write polished prose and had won an early reputation.

sentences.zh: 師事譙周，周門人稱為子貢。

translations.literal: He studied under Qiao Zhou, and Zhou's disciples called him Zigong.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under Qiao Zhou, whose students nicknamed him Zigong after Confucius's disciple.

sentences.zh: 性方亮嚴整，待士無倦，輕財好施，不營產業。

translations.literal: In nature upright, bright, strict, and orderly, he treated gentlemen tirelessly, was light with wealth and fond of giving, and did not engage in building estates.
translations.idiomatic: He was upright, principled, and disciplined, treated scholars with inexhaustible courtesy, cared little for money and gave freely, and never bothered to amass property.

sentences.zh: 仕蜀為太子舍人、宣信校尉。

translations.literal: He served Shu as Gentleman Attendant of the Heir Apparent and Colonel Who Inspires Faith.
translations.idiomatic: Under Shu he held the posts of Gentleman Attendant of the Heir Apparent and Colonel Who Inspires Faith.

sentences.zh: 再使于吳，吳人稱焉。

translations.literal: Twice he was sent as envoy to Wu, and the people of Wu praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Sent twice as envoy to Wu, he earned high praise there.

sentences.zh: 時黃皓預政，眾多附之，憲獨介然。

translations.literal: At the time Huang Hao intervened in government, and the multitude attached themselves to him; Xian alone stood apart unyielding.
translations.idiomatic: When the eunuch Huang Hao dominated the court and most officials curried favor, Xian alone held himself aloof.

sentences.zh: 皓恚之，左遷巴東太守。

translations.literal: Hao resented him and demoted him to Administrator of Badong.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Hao resented him and had him relegated to Administrator of Badong.

sentences.zh: 時大將軍閻宇都督巴東，拜憲領軍，為宇副貳。

translations.literal: At the time Grand General Yan Yu supervised Badong; Xian was appointed to command the army as Yu's second-in-command.
translations.idiomatic: Grand General Yan Yu then commanded the Badong theater; Xian was named army commander and served as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 魏之伐蜀，召宇西還，憲守永安城。

translations.literal: When Wei attacked Shu, Yu was summoned back west, and Xian defended Yong'an city.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei invaded Shu, Yan Yu was recalled westward, leaving Xian to hold Yong'an.

sentences.zh: 及成都敗，城中擾動，邊江長吏皆棄城走，憲斬亂者一人，百姓乃安。

translations.literal: When Chengdu fell, the city was disturbed; all the river-border senior officials abandoned the cities and fled. Xian executed one who stirred disorder, and the common people then were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: After Chengdu fell, the garrison panicked and magistrates along the river fled their posts; Xian executed one ringleader of the unrest and restored calm among the people.

sentences.zh: 知劉禪降，乃率所統臨於都亭三日。

translations.literal: Learning that Liu Shan had surrendered, he then led those under his command to mourn at the metropolitan pavilion for three days.
translations.idiomatic: When he learned that Liu Shan had surrendered, he led his troops to the metropolitan pavilion and mourned there for three days.

sentences.zh: 吳聞蜀敗，遣將軍盛憲西上，外托救援，內欲襲憲。

translations.literal: Wu heard that Shu had been defeated and sent General Sheng Xian westward, outwardly claiming relief but inwardly intending to surprise Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of Shu's collapse, Wu dispatched General Sheng Xian upriver under the pretense of rescue while actually planning to seize Xian's position.

sentences.zh: 憲曰：「本朝傾覆，吳為脣齒，不恤我難，而邀其利，吾寧當為降虜乎！

translations.literal: Xian said: "Our dynasty has overturned; Wu is lip and teeth with us. They do not pity our hardship but seek profit—how could I consent to become a captive who surrenders!"
translations.idiomatic: Xian declared: "Our state has fallen; Wu ought to be our ally. Instead of helping us in our distress, they mean to profit from it—do they think I will simply surrender and become their prisoner?"

sentences.zh: 」乃歸順。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he submitted to allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore submitted to the Jin regime.

sentences.zh: 於是繕甲完聚，厲以節義，士皆用命。

translations.literal: Thereupon he repaired armor, completed gathering stores, and urged them with integrity and righteousness; the soldiers all obeyed orders.
translations.idiomatic: He then repaired arms and provisioned the defense, rallied his men with appeals to duty and honor, and every soldier obeyed without hesitation.

sentences.zh: 及鐘會、鄧艾死，百城無主，吳又使步協西征，憲大破其軍。

translations.literal: When Zhong Hui and Deng Ai died, the hundred cities had no master; Wu again sent Bu Xie on a western expedition, and Xian greatly defeated his army.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhong Hui and Deng Ai were dead and cities throughout the region lacked reliable rulers, Wu sent Bu Xie west again; Xian routed his force decisively.

sentences.zh: 孫休怒，又遣陸抗助協。

translations.literal: Sun Xiu was angry and again sent Lu Kang to assist Xie.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xiu flew into a rage and dispatched Lu Kang to reinforce Bu Xie.

sentences.zh: 憲距守經年，救援不至，城中疾疫太半。

translations.literal: Xian resisted and defended for a full year; relief did not arrive, and more than half in the city suffered plague.
translations.idiomatic: Xian held out for over a year without reinforcements while plague carried off more than half the garrison.

sentences.zh: 或勸南出牂柯，北奔上庸，可以保全。

translations.literal: Some urged going south out through Zangke or fleeing north to Shangyong, by which one could preserve completeness.
translations.idiomatic: Some advised retreating south into Zangke or north toward Shangyong to save themselves.

sentences.zh: 憲曰：「夫為人主，百姓所仰，既不能存，急而棄之，君子不為也。

translations.literal: Xian said: "One who is lord for the people is what the hundred surnames rely on; if one cannot preserve them and in urgency abandons them, a gentleman does not do this."
translations.idiomatic: Xian replied: "The people look to their commander for protection. To abandon them in a crisis because you cannot save them—that is not what a gentleman does."

sentences.zh: 畢命於此矣。

translations.literal: I shall exhaust my life here."
translations.idiomatic: I will see this duty through to the end, here."

sentences.zh: 」會荊州刺史胡烈等救之，抗退。

translations.literal: " At that time Jing Province Inspector Hu Lie and others rescued him, and Kang withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Then Jing Province Inspector Hu Lie arrived with relief, and Lu Kang pulled back.

sentences.zh: 加陵江將軍、監巴東軍事、使持節，領武陵太守。

translations.literal: He was additionally appointed General Who Crosses the Jiang, Supervisor of Military Affairs in Badong, Bearer of the Credential and Staff, and Concurrent Administrator of Wuling.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to General Who Crosses the Jiang, given supervisory authority over Badong military affairs with insignia and staff, and concurrently named Administrator of Wuling.

sentences.zh: 泰始初入朝，詔曰：「憲忠烈果毅，有才策器幹，可給鼓吹。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Taishi era he entered court; an edict said: "Xian is loyal, fierce, resolute, and daring; he has talent, stratagem, and capability; he may be granted drum and flute bands."
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taishi reign he was summoned to the capital; an imperial rescript praised his loyalty, courage, and decisiveness, noted his strategic gifts and administrative grit, and authorized the honor of a military band.

sentences.zh: 」又賜山玄玉佩劍。

translations.literal: " He was also granted a sword with a mountain-pattern dark jade pendant.
translations.idiomatic: He also received a sword fitted with a dark jade pendant carved in mountain pattern.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈使持節、安南將軍、武陵太守，追封西鄂侯，諡曰烈。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he was awarded Bearer of the Credential and Staff, General Who Pacifies the South, and Administrator of Wuling; posthumously enfeoffed as Marquis of Xi'e; posthumous title Lie, read as fiercest valor.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously honored as Bearer of Staff with full powers, General Who Pacifies the South, and Administrator of Wuling, enfeoffed posthumously as Marquis of Xi'e, and given the posthumous epithet Lie, "the Fierce."

sentences.zh: 初，憲侍宴華林園，詔問蜀大臣子弟，後問先輩宜時敘用者，憲薦蜀人常忌、杜軫等，皆西國之良器，武帝並召而任之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Xian attended a banquet in the Huilin Garden, an edict asked about sons and younger brothers of Shu great ministers, afterward asking about elders suitable for timely appointment and employment; Xian recommended Shu men Chang Ji, Du Zhen, and others; all were fine vessels of the western state; Emperor Wu summoned and employed them all.
translations.idiomatic: Once, while attending a banquet in the Huilin Garden, Xian was questioned by imperial order about younger relatives of Shu's leading ministers and then about senior worthies who ought to be employed without delay; he nominated Chang Ji, Du Zhen, and others from Shu—all outstanding talents of the former western kingdom—and Emperor Wu summoned each of them to office.

sentences.zh: 子襲，曆給事中、陵江將軍，統其父部曲，至廣漢太守。

translations.literal: His son Xi successively served as Palace Attendant and General Who Crosses the Jiang, commanded his father's personal troops, and rose to Administrator of Guanghan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xi rose through the offices of Palace Attendant and General Who Crosses the Jiang, inherited command of his father's household troops, and eventually became Administrator of Guanghan.

sentences.zh: 兄子尚。

translations.literal: His elder brother's son Shang.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Shang.

translations.literal: Equals sign, table continuation marker.
translations.idiomatic: Section divider in the tabular layout.

sentences.zh: 兄子尚

translations.literal: Brother's son Shang.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Shang.

sentences.zh: =尚字敬之，一名仲。

translations.literal: "= Shang, courtesy name Jingzhi, also named Zhong."
translations.idiomatic: Luo Shang, courtesy name Jingzhi, also known as Zhong.

sentences.zh: 父式，牂柯太守。

translations.literal: His father Shi was Administrator of Zangke.
translations.idiomatic: His father, Luo Shi, had been Administrator of Zangke.

sentences.zh: 尚少孤，依叔父憲。

translations.literal: Shang was orphaned young and relied on his uncle Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he was raised under his uncle Luo Xian.

sentences.zh: 善屬文。

translations.literal: He was good at composing essays.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote excellent prose.

sentences.zh: 荊州刺史王戎以尚及劉喬為參軍，並委任之。

translations.literal: Jing Province Inspector Wang Rong employed Shang and Liu Qiao as staff advisers and entrusted them equally.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rong, Inspector of Jing Province, appointed both Shang and Liu Qiao as military advisers and relied on them fully.

sentences.zh: 太康末，為梁州刺史。

translations.literal: At the end of the Taikang era he became Inspector of Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Toward the end of the Taikang era he was named Inspector of Liang Province.

sentences.zh: 及趙廞反于蜀，尚表曰：「廞非雄才，必無所成，計日聽其敗耳。

translations.literal: When Zhao Xin rebelled in Shu, Shang submitted a memorial saying: "Xin is not a heroic talent; he will certainly accomplish nothing; count the days until we hear of his defeat."
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Xin rose in rebellion in Shu, Shang memorialized: "Xin lacks real ability; he is bound to fail—we need only wait for news of his collapse."

sentences.zh: 」乃假尚節為平西將軍、益州刺史、西戎校尉。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Shang was lent insignia as General Who Pacifies the West, Inspector of Yi Province, and Colonel of the Western Rong.
translations.idiomatic: The court therefore invested him with ceremonial credentials as General Who Pacifies the West, Inspector of Yi Province, and Colonel of the Western Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 性貪，少斷，蜀人言曰：「尚之所愛，非邪則佞，尚之所憎，非忠則正。

translations.literal: His nature was greedy and lacked decisiveness; the people of Shu said: "Those whom Shang favors are either wicked or flattering; those whom Shang detests are either loyal or upright."
translations.idiomatic: Greedy and indecisive, he drew this proverb from the people of Shu: "Those Shang favors are crooks or sycophants; those he hates are the loyal and the upright."

sentences.zh: 富擬魯、衛，家成市里；

translations.literal: Their wealth rivals Lu and Wei; their households fill the market wards."
translations.idiomatic: Their fortunes rival small kingdoms; their mansions crowd the streets."

sentences.zh: 貪如豺狼，無復極已。

translations.literal: Greedy as jackals and wolves, there is no limit."
translations.idiomatic: They are ravenous as wolves, with greed that knows no bound."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「蜀賊尚可，羅尚殺我。

translations.literal: " Again they said: "The Shu bandits one could still bear; Luo Shang kills us."
translations.idiomatic: Another rhyme ran: "We could endure the Shu rebels—Luo Shang is what kills us."

sentences.zh: 平西將軍，反更為禍。

translations.literal: The General Who Pacifies the West instead becomes a calamity."
translations.idiomatic: The 'General Who Pacifies the West' brings worse disaster still."

sentences.zh: 」時李特亦起於蜀，攻蜀，殺趙廞。

translations.literal: " At that time Li Te also rose in Shu, attacked Shu, and killed Zhao Xin.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Li Te had risen in Shu, marched against Zhao Xin, and killed him.

sentences.zh: 又攻尚于成都，尚退保江陽，初，尚乞師方岳，荊州刺史宗岱率建平太守孫阜救之，次於江州，岱、阜兵盛，諸為寇所逼者，人有奮志。

translations.literal: Again he attacked Shang at Chengdu; Shang withdrew to defend Jiangyang. Earlier, Shang had begged troops from the regional governors; Jing Province Inspector Zong Dai led Jianping Administrator Sun Fu to rescue him and halted at Jiangzhou; Dai's and Fu's troops were strong, and among those pressed by the bandits, each person had a mind to exert themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Li Te then assaulted Shang at Chengdu, forcing him back to Jiangyang. Shang had earlier appealed to the provincial governors for aid: Zong Dai of Jing Province brought Sun Fu, Administrator of Jianping, as reinforcements, and they encamped at Jiangzhou. With Dai and Fu commanding a powerful force, everyone trapped by the rebels found new courage.

sentences.zh: 尚乃使兵曹從事任銳偽降，因出密宣告於外，克日俱擊，遂大破之，斬李特，傳首洛陽。

translations.literal: Shang then had Ren Rui, his Clerk of the Bureau of Military Affairs, pretend to surrender; thereby he issued secret proclamations outside, fixed a day for a joint strike, and thereby greatly defeated them, executed Li Te, and sent his head to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Shang ordered Ren Rui, a clerk in his military bureau, to feign defection; Ren slipped word of the plan to allies outside, coordinated a timed assault, and routed Li Te's army. Li Te was beheaded and his head sent to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 特子雄僭號，都於郫城。

translations.literal: Te's son Xiong presumptuously assumed a dynastic title and made his capital at Pi city.
translations.idiomatic: Li Te's son Li Xiong then proclaimed himself ruler and established his capital at Pi.

sentences.zh: 尚遣將軍隗伯攻之，不克。

translations.literal: Shang sent General Wei Bo to attack him and did not conquer.
translations.idiomatic: Shang dispatched General Wei Bo against him but failed to take the city.

sentences.zh: 俄而尚卒，雄遂據有蜀土。

translations.literal: Soon Shang died; Xiong thereupon occupied Shu territory.
translations.idiomatic: Shang died not long afterward, and Li Xiong soon controlled all of Shu.

sentences.zh: 滕修

translations.literal: Teng Xiu — biography heading.
translations.idiomatic: Teng Xiu.

sentences.zh: 滕修，字顯先，南陽西鄂人也。

translations.literal: Teng Xiu, courtesy name Xianxian, was a native of Xi'e in Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Teng Xiu, courtesy name Xianxian, hailed from Xi'e in Nanyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 仕吳為將帥，封西鄂侯。

translations.literal: He served Wu as a general and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xi'e.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wu he rose to general's rank and received the marquisate of Xi'e.

sentences.zh: 孫皓時，代熊睦為廣州刺史，甚有威惠。

translations.literal: Under Sun Hao he replaced Xiong Mu as Inspector of Guang Province and had great awe-inspiring kindness.
translations.idiomatic: During Sun Hao's reign he succeeded Xiong Mu as Inspector of Guang Province and ruled there with a formidable yet benevolent hand.

sentences.zh: 徵為執金吾。

translations.literal: He was summoned to be Bearer of the Mace.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to the capital as Bearer of the Mace.

sentences.zh: 廣州部曲督郭馬等為亂，皓以修宿有威惠，為嶺表所伏，以為使持節、都督廣州軍事、鎮南將軍、廣州牧以討之。

translations.literal: Guangzhou's troop supervisor Guo Ma and others made rebellion; Hao, because Xiu long had awe-inspiring kindness and was submitted to by the Lingnan region, appointed him Bearer of the Credential and Staff, Supervisor of Military Affairs of Guang Province, General Who Guards the South, and Shepherd of Guang Province to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: When Guo Ma and other local commanders mutinied in Guangzhou, Sun Hao turned to Xiu—whose prestige and fair dealing had long won the south's respect—and commissioned him with full credentials as commander of Guang forces, General Who Guards the South, and Governor of Guangzhou to suppress the revolt.

sentences.zh: 未克而王師伐吳，修率眾赴難。

translations.literal: Before he had conquered, the royal army attacked Wu; Xiu led the multitude to go to the difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could finish the campaign, Jin's imperial army invaded Wu; Xiu marched his troops east to answer the crisis.

sentences.zh: 至巴丘而皓已降，乃縞素流涕而還，與廣州刺史閭豐、蒼梧太守王毅各送印綬，詔以修為安南將軍，廣州牧、持節、都督如故，封武當侯，加鼓吹，委以南方事。

translations.literal: He reached Baqiu when Hao had already surrendered; then in plain white he wept and flowed tears and returned, and with Guang Province Inspector Lu Feng and Cangwu Administrator Wang Yi each sent in seals and ribbons; an edict appointed Xiu as General Who Pacifies the South, Shepherd of Guang Province, Bearer of Insignia, Supervisor as before, enfeoffed as Marquis of Wudang, granted drum and flute bands, and entrusted him with southern affairs.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he reached Baqiu, Sun Hao had already capitulated. Xiu turned back in mourning dress, weeping openly. He joined Guangzhou Inspector Lu Feng and Cangwu Prefect Wang Yi in surrendering their seals to Jin. The court confirmed him as General Who Pacifies the South and Governor of Guangzhou with unchanged military authority, enfeoffed him as Marquis of Wudang, awarded him an honorary band, and left southern affairs in his hands.

sentences.zh: 修在南積年，為邊夷所附。

translations.literal: Xiu was in the south many years and was attached to by border barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: He spent years in the south, where frontier peoples willingly rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 卒，請葬京師，帝嘉其意，賜墓田一頃，諡曰聲。

translations.literal: He died, requesting burial in the capital; the Emperor praised his intent and granted one qing of tomb land; posthumous title Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he asked to be buried near the capital; the emperor approved the gesture, granted a hectare of burial ground, and gave him the posthumous name Sheng.

sentences.zh: 修之子並上表曰：「亡父修羈絏吳壤，為所驅馳；

translations.literal: Xiu's sons Bing submitted a memorial saying: "Our deceased father Xiu was bound in Wu territory and was driven to gallop for them;
translations.idiomatic: His sons, led by Bing, petitioned: "Our late father served Wu under constraint, forced to do its bidding;

sentences.zh: 幸逢開通，沐浴至化，得從俘虜握戎馬之要；

translations.literal: fortunately encountering opening and communication, bathing in the utmost transformation, he was able from captives to grasp the essentials of war-horses;
translations.idiomatic: he was fortunate to live to see unification and bathe in your sagely influence, rising even from the ranks of the conquered to hold military command;

sentences.zh: 未覲聖顏，委南籓之重，實由勳勞少聞天聽故也。

translations.literal: not having gazed on the sage countenance, being entrusted with the weight of the southern frontier, was truly because his merit and toil were seldom heard in Heaven's hearing."
translations.idiomatic: yet he never once looked upon Your Majesty's face before shouldering the defense of the south—solely because his service went largely unheard at court."

sentences.zh: 年衰疾篤，屢乞骸骨，未蒙垂哀，奄至薨隕。

translations.literal: Years declining, illness severe, repeatedly begging for bones, not receiving downward pity, suddenly reaching death and fall.
translations.idiomatic: Age and illness wore him down; he repeatedly asked permission to retire but received no imperial sympathy, and suddenly he was gone.

sentences.zh: 臣承遺意，輿櫬還都，瞻望雲闕，實懷痛裂。

translations.literal: Your servants inheriting his dying intent, carried the bier back to the capital; gazing toward the cloud palace, our bosoms truly hold pain that splits."
translations.idiomatic: We honored his last wish and bore his coffin to the capital; gazing toward the palace gates, our grief is unbearable."

sentences.zh: 竊聞博士諡修曰聲，直彰流播，不稱行績，不勝愚情，冒昧聞訴。

translations.literal: We privately hear the Academician posthumously titled Xiu Sheng; straightforward manifestation spreads abroad, not matching deeds and traces; unable to overcome foolish feeling, we venture to hear and appeal."
translations.idiomatic: We understand the court scholars assigned him the posthumous name Sheng, but that label hardly reflects his true achievements; we cannot bear the injustice and presume to appeal."

sentences.zh: 」帝乃賜諡曰忠。

translations.literal: " The Emperor then bestowed posthumous title Zhong, meaning loyal.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thereupon changed his posthumous epithet to Zhong, "the Loyal."

sentences.zh: 並子含，初為庾冰輕車長史，討蘇峻有功，封夏陽縣開國侯，邑千六百戶，授平南將軍、廣州刺史。

translations.literal: Bing's son Han, initially was Yu Bing's light-chariot senior secretary; attacking Su Jun he had merit, was enfeoffed as Marquis who Opens the State of Xiayang with 1,600 households, and was appointed General Who Pacifies the South and Inspector of Guang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Bing's son Han first served as chief clerk on Yu Bing's light-chariot staff; he distinguished himself in the campaign against Su Jun and was enfeoffed as founding marquis of Xiayang with sixteen hundred households, then named General Who Pacifies the South and Inspector of Guang Province.

sentences.zh: 在任積年，甚有威惠，卒諡曰戴。

translations.literal: In office many years, he had great awe-inspiring kindness; when he died posthumous title Dai.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Guangzhou for years with the same blend of authority and generosity, and at his death received the posthumous epithet Dai.

sentences.zh: 含弟子遁，交州刺史。

translations.literal: Han's younger brother's son Dun was Inspector of Jiao Province.
translations.idiomatic: Han's nephew Dun later became Inspector of Jiao Province.

sentences.zh: 修曾孫恬之，龍驤將軍、魏郡太守，戍黎陽，為翟遼所執，死之。

translations.literal: Xiu's great-grandson Tianzhi was General of Agile Cavalry and Administrator of Wei Commandery; garrisoning Liyang, he was seized by Zhai Liao and died for it.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu's great-grandson Tianzhi served as General of Agile Cavalry and Wei Commandery prefect; holding Liyang, he was captured by Zhai Liao and killed.

sentences.zh: 馬隆

translations.literal: Ma Long — biography heading.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Long.

sentences.zh: 馬隆，字孝興，東平平陸人。

translations.literal: Ma Long, courtesy name Xiaoxing, was a native of Pinglu in Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Long, courtesy name Xiaoxing, came from Pinglu in Dongping kingdom.

sentences.zh: 少而智勇，好立名節。

translations.literal: In youth he was wise and brave and fond of establishing name and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a youth he showed courage and good sense and cared deeply for honor.

sentences.zh: 魏兗州刺史令狐愚坐事伏誅，舉州無敢收者。

translations.literal: Wei's Yan Province Inspector Linghu Yu sat on an affair and was executed by law; the whole province had none who dared collect him.
translations.idiomatic: When Linghu Yu, Inspector of Yan Province, was executed for conspiracy, no one in the province dared claim his body.

sentences.zh: 隆以武吏托稱愚客，以私財殯葬，服喪三年，列植松柏，禮畢乃還，一州以為美談。

translations.literal: Long as a military clerk falsely claimed to be Yu's guest, used private wealth to bury, observed mourning three years, lined plant pines and cypresses, when rites finished then returned; the whole province took it as fine talk.
translations.idiomatic: Long, a minor military clerk, presented himself as Yu's retainer, paid for the funeral out of his own pocket, and mourned three years, planting pines and cypresses on the grave before returning to duty. The story became legend throughout the province.

sentences.zh: 署武猛從事。

translations.literal: He was appointed Attendant Clerk for Military Ferocity.
translations.idiomatic: He was named adjutant for military affairs.

sentences.zh: 泰始中，將興伐吳之役，下詔曰：「吳會未平，宜得猛士以濟武功。

translations.literal: In Taishi, about to raise the campaign to attack Wu, an edict was issued saying: "Wu and Kuaiji are not yet pacified; it is fitting to obtain fierce warriors to aid military merit."
translations.idiomatic: During the Taishi era, as the court prepared to conquer Wu, an edict declared: "The southeast still resists; we need bold fighters to finish the work."

sentences.zh: 雖舊有薦舉之法，未足以盡殊才。

translations.literal: Although there is the old law of recommendation and raising, it is not sufficient to exhaust extraordinary talent.
translations.idiomatic: The usual recommendation system alone cannot surface every exceptional man.

sentences.zh: 其普告州郡，有壯勇秀異才力傑出者，皆以名聞，將簡其尤異，擢而用之。

translations.literal: Generally proclaim to provinces and commanderies: those who have stalwart bravery, outstanding excellence, strength and talent standing out, all report by name; we will select their utmost excellence and promote and employ them.
translations.idiomatic: Let every province and commandery be notified: anyone of unusual courage or strength is to be nominated by name so the throne can pick the best and elevate them.

sentences.zh: 苟有其人，勿限所取。

translations.literal: If there are such persons, do not limit where they are taken from."
translations.idiomatic: Where such men exist, no origin should disqualify them."

sentences.zh: 」兗州舉隆才堪良將。

translations.literal: " Yan Province recommended Long's talent as sufficient for a fine general.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Province nominated Ma Long as qualified to serve as a general.

sentences.zh: 稍遷司馬督。

translations.literal: Gradually he was promoted to Supervisor of the Major's Office.
translations.idiomatic: He was gradually promoted to oversee the marshal's office.

sentences.zh: 初，涼州刺史楊欣失羌戎之和，隆陳其必敗。

translations.literal: Earlier, Liang Province Inspector Yang Xin lost harmony with the Qiang and Rong; Long stated that he would certainly be defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Long had warned that Yang Xin, Inspector of Liang Province, was alienating the Qiang and other tribes—a policy bound to end in disaster.

sentences.zh: 俄而欣為虜所沒，河西斷絕，帝每有西顧之憂，臨朝而歎曰：「誰能為我討此虜通涼州者乎？

translations.literal: Soon Xin was swallowed by the barbarians; Hexi was cut off; the Emperor often had anxiety of looking west; facing court he sighed saying: "Who can for me attack these barbarians and open Liang Province?"
translations.idiomatic: Xin was soon overrun by tribesmen, and communications with Hexi collapsed. The emperor faced the court with a worried gaze westward and asked, "Who will clear these bandits away and reopen the road to Liangzhou for me?"

sentences.zh: 」朝臣莫對。

translations.literal: " Court ministers none answered.
translations.idiomatic: The assembly had no answer.

sentences.zh: 隆進曰：「陛下若能任臣，臣能平之。

translations.literal: Long stepped forward saying: "If Your Majesty can employ your servant, your servant can pacify them."
translations.idiomatic: Ma Long stepped forward: "Employ me, Your Majesty, and I will pacify them."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「必能滅賊，何為不任，顧卿方略何如耳。

translations.literal: " The Emperor said: "If you can certainly destroy the bandits, why not employ—only what is your stratagem like?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "If you can destroy them, why would I refuse? I only want to hear your plan."

sentences.zh: 隆曰：「陛下若能任臣，當聽臣自任。

translations.literal: Long said: "If Your Majesty can employ your servant, you ought to listen to your servant self-employ."
translations.idiomatic: Long said: "If you trust me, you must let me choose my own men and methods."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「云何？

translations.literal: " The Emperor said: "How?"
translations.idiomatic: "In what way?" asked the emperor.

sentences.zh: 隆曰：「臣請募勇士三千人，無問所從來，率之鼓行而西，稟陛下威德，醜虜何足滅哉！

translations.literal: Long said: "Your servant requests to recruit three thousand fierce warriors, without asking where they come from, lead them drum-marching west, relying on Your Majesty's awe-inspiring virtue—how are ugly barbarians worth destroying!"
translations.idiomatic: "Let me raise three thousand volunteers," Long answered, "origin irrelevant; I will march them west with drums beating. Under your majesty's prestige, those wretches will be swept aside."

sentences.zh: 」帝許之，乃以隆為武威太守。

translations.literal: " The Emperor permitted it; thereupon he appointed Long as Administrator of Wuwei.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and named him Administrator of Wuwei.

sentences.zh: 公卿僉曰：「六軍既眾，州郡兵多，但當用之，不宜橫設賞募以亂常典。

translations.literal: The dukes and ministers all said: "The six armies are already numerous; province and commandery troops are many—only ought to use them; it is not fitting to recklessly establish rewards and recruitment to disorder constant statutes."
translations.idiomatic: Ministers protested: "We already have massive imperial armies and provincial forces—use those; ad hoc bounties and private levies only undermine regulations."

sentences.zh: 隆小將妄說，不可從也。

translations.literal: Long is a petty general speaking wildly; he cannot be followed."
translations.idiomatic: Ma Long is a junior officer talking nonsense—ignore him."

sentences.zh: 」帝弗納。

translations.literal: " The Emperor did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor brushed their objections aside.

sentences.zh: 隆募限腰引弩三十六鈞、弓四鈞，立標簡試。

translations.literal: Long recruited limiting waist-draw crossbow thirty-six jun, bow four jun, erected markers and selected by testing.
translations.idiomatic: Long recruited men who could draw a thirty-six-jun crossbow with the waist and a four-jun bow, posting standards and testing applicants.

sentences.zh: 自旦至中，得三千五百人，隆曰：「足矣。

translations.literal: From dawn to midday he obtained three thousand five hundred men; Long said: "It is enough."
translations.idiomatic: From dawn until noon he signed up thirty-five hundred recruits. "That will do," said Long.

sentences.zh: 」因請自至武庫選杖。

translations.literal: He thereupon requested personally to go to the armory to select staffs.
translations.idiomatic: He asked permission to pick his own issue from the imperial armory.

sentences.zh: 武庫令與隆忿爭，御史中丞奏劾隆，隆曰：「臣當亡命戰場，以報所受，武庫令乃以魏時朽杖見給，不可復用，非陛下使臣滅賊意也。

translations.literal: The armory director quarreled angrily with Long; the Palace Assistant Imperial Clerk impeached Long. Long said: "Your servant ought to lose life on the battlefield to repay what he has received; the armory director however supplied rotten staffs from Wei times, unusable any longer—this is not Your Majesty's intent in sending your servant to destroy the bandits."
translations.idiomatic: The armory chief quarreled with Long and denounced him to the censorate. Long replied: "I expect to stake my life on the frontier in return for your trust; instead I am handed rotten poles left over from Wei—unfit for combat—hardly what Your Majesty meant by ordering me to crush the enemy."

sentences.zh: 」帝從之，又給其三年軍資。

translations.literal: " The Emperor followed him and furthermore supplied three years of army provisions.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved and issued three years' worth of military supplies.

sentences.zh: 隆於是西渡溫水。

translations.literal: Long thereupon crossed the Wen River westward.
translations.idiomatic: Long then led his men west across the Wen River.

sentences.zh: 虜樹機能等以眾萬計，或乘險以遏隆前，或設伏以截隆後。

translations.literal: The barbarians Tufa Shujineng and others, numbering in the tens of thousands by estimate, some exploited narrows to block Long's front, some laid ambushes to cut Long's rear.
translations.idiomatic: Shujineng's tribesmen, perhaps ten thousand strong, sometimes held the defiles to bar Long's advance, sometimes ambushed his rear.

sentences.zh: 隆依八陣圖作偏箱車，地廣則鹿角車營，路狹則為木屋施于車上，且戰且前，弓矢所及，應弦而倒。

translations.literal: Long according to the Eight Formations diagram made covered-wing carts; where the ground was wide he used antler-carts in camp formation; where the road was narrow he built wooden huts set on the carts, fighting while advancing; wherever bow and arrow reached, they fell at the twang of the string.
translations.idiomatic: Following the Eight Arrays formation, he deployed winged baggage carts; on open ground he ringed his camp with antler barriers, in narrow passes he mounted wooden fighting towers on the wagons, fighting his way forward so that every arrow found its mark.

sentences.zh: 奇謀間發，出敵不意。

translations.literal: Strange stratagems broke out intermittently, emerging beyond the enemy's expectation.
translations.idiomatic: He struck again with unexpected tactics that caught the enemy off guard.

sentences.zh: 或夾道累磁石，賊負鐵鎧，行不得前，隆卒悉被犀甲，無所留礙，賊咸以為神。

translations.literal: Sometimes he piled lodestone along the road; the bandits bore iron armor and could not advance; Long's soldiers all wore rhinoceros hide armor and had nothing to snag them; the bandits all thought it supernatural.
translations.idiomatic: At one point he laid magnets along the trail: the enemy wore iron mail and stalled helplessly, while his own men wore rhinoceros-hide lamellar and advanced freely—the tribesmen decided he commanded spirits.

sentences.zh: 轉戰千里，殺傷以千數。

translations.literal: He fought shifting battles a thousand li, killing and wounding by the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned a thousand li, inflicting thousands of casualties.

sentences.zh: 自隆之西，音問斷絕，朝廷憂之，或謂已沒。

translations.literal: From the time Long went west, communication broke off; the court worried, and some said he had already perished.
translations.idiomatic: Once Long marched west, contact ceased; the court feared the worst and rumors spread that he was dead.

sentences.zh: 後隆使夜到，帝撫掌歡笑。

translations.literal: Later Long's messenger arrived by night; the Emperor clapped his palms and laughed with joy.
translations.idiomatic: When Long's courier reached the capital by night, the emperor clapped his hands and laughed aloud.

sentences.zh: 詰朝，召群臣謂曰：「若從諸卿言，是無秦、涼也。

translations.literal: At the next dawn he summoned the ministers and said to them: "If we had followed you gentlemen's words, there would be no Qin or Liang."
translations.idiomatic: At dawn he told his ministers: "Had I listened to you, Qinzhou and Liangzhou would be lost."

sentences.zh: 」乃詔曰：「隆以偏師寡眾，奮不顧難，冒險能濟。

translations.literal: " He then issued an edict saying: "Long with a detached army and outnumbered host exerted himself heedless of hardship, braved danger and was able to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: A rescript followed: "Ma Long, outnumbered and leading only a side force, risked everything and broke through."

sentences.zh: 其假節、宣威將軍，加赤幢、曲蓋、鼓吹。

translations.literal: Let him be lent insignia, General Who Spreads Might, and granted crimson canopy, curved parasol, and drum band."
translations.idiomatic: He was granted credential insignia as General Who Spreads Might, with crimson command canopy, curved parasol, and an honorary band.

sentences.zh: 」隆到武威，虜大人猝跋韓、且萬能等率萬餘落歸降，前後誅殺及降附者以萬計。

translations.literal: " When Long reached Wuwei, the barbarian elders Cupohan and Qieneng led more than ten thousand yurt households to submit; those executed, killed, surrendered, and attached in succession numbered in the tens of thousands by estimate.
translations.idiomatic: At Wuwei, tribal chiefs such as Cupohan and Qieneng brought over ten thousand camps to surrender; his cumulative kills and admissions ran into the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 又率善戎沒骨能等與樹機能大戰，斬之，涼州遂平。

translations.literal: He also led the good Rong Mobegineng and others to fight a great battle with Shujineng, executed him, and Liang Province was thereupon pacified.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined loyal auxiliaries led by Mobegineng to crush Shujineng in a decisive battle; with Shujineng dead, Liangzhou was finally quiet.

sentences.zh: 朝議將加隆將士勳賞，有司奏隆將士皆先加顯爵，不應更授，衛將軍楊珧駁曰：「前精募將士，少加爵命者，此適所以為誘引。

translations.literal: Court deliberation was about to add merit rewards for Long's officers and soldiers; the relevant office reported that Long's officers and soldiers had all already received prominent noble ranks and ought not receive further investiture. General of the Guard Yang Yao objected: "Earlier the finely recruited officers and soldiers received slight advancement in noble rank—this was precisely how they were enticed."
translations.idiomatic: The ministry argued Long's men already held high titles and deserved no second grant. Yang Yao of the guards rejoined: "Those earlier promotions were only bait for recruits."

sentences.zh: 今隆全軍獨克，西土獲安，不得便以前授塞此後功，宜皆聽許，以明要信。

translations.literal: " Now Long's whole army alone conquered; the western lands obtained peace—one cannot conveniently use the earlier grants to block these later merits; it is fitting all be permitted, to clarify essential trust."
translations.idiomatic: "Now Long's army alone finished the campaign and secured the west; prior commissions must not cancel today's rewards—grant every petition to show the throne keeps its word."

sentences.zh: 」乃從珧議，賜爵加秩各有差。

translations.literal: " Thereupon they followed Yao's deliberation; noble titles and salary ranks were conferred each according to degree.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted Yang Yao's advice and distributed noble ranks and stipends accordingly.

sentences.zh: 太康初，朝廷以西平荒毀，宜時興復，以隆為平虜護軍、西平太守，將所領精兵，又給牙門一軍，屯據西平。

translations.literal: Early in the Taikang era the court, because Xiping was ruined and waste, deemed it proper to restore it in timely fashion; it appointed Long as Protector Who Pacifies the Caitiffs and Administrator of Xiping, leading his elite troops, and furthermore supplied one Ya Gate corps, garrisoning and occupying Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taikang the court decided ruined Xiping must be rebuilt and named Long Protector Who Pacifies the Caitiffs and prefect there, reinforced with picked troops plus a full Ya Gate brigade to hold the city.

sentences.zh: 時南虜成奚每為邊患，隆至，帥軍討之。

translations.literal: At the time the southern barbarian Cheng Xi constantly made border trouble; when Long arrived, he led the army to strike him.
translations.idiomatic: When the southern tribesman Cheng Xi kept raiding the frontier, Long marched out and attacked him.

sentences.zh: 虜據險距守，隆令軍士皆負農器，將若田者。

translations.literal: The barbarians held narrows and resisted defense; Long ordered the soldiers all to carry farm tools as if they were going to till fields.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy held the heights; Long had every soldier shoulder hoes and spades like farmers heading for the fields.

sentences.zh: 虜以隆無征討意，禦眾稍怠。

translations.literal: The barbarians thought Long had no intent of campaigning and punishing; they guarded the multitude somewhat slackly.
translations.idiomatic: Assuming he planned no offensive, they relaxed their guard.

sentences.zh: 隆因其無備，進兵擊破之。

translations.literal: Long because they were unprepared advanced troops and struck and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Long seized their complacency and smashed their position.

sentences.zh: 畢隆之政，不敢為寇。

translations.literal: Through to the completion of Long's administration they did not dare act as bandits.
translations.idiomatic: For the rest of Long's tenure they never raided again.

sentences.zh: 太熙初，封奉高縣侯，加授東羌校尉。

translations.literal: Early in the Taixi era he was enfeoffed Marquis of Fenggao and additionally appointed Colonel of the Eastern Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Taixi he received the marquisate of Fenggao and the colonelcy over the Eastern Qiang.

sentences.zh: 積十餘年，威信震於隴右。

translations.literal: Accumulating more than ten years, awe-inspiring trust shook Longyou.
translations.idiomatic: After a decade his prestige dominated the Longyou region.

sentences.zh: 時略陽太守馮翊嚴舒與楊駿通親，蜜圖代隆，毀隆年老謬耄，不宜服戎，於是征隆，以舒代鎮。

translations.literal: At the time the Administrator of Lüeyang from Pingyi, Yan Shu, had marriage ties with Yang Jun and secretly plotted to replace Long; he slandered Long as old in years, mistaken and senile, unsuited to bearing arms; thereupon Long was summoned and Shu substituted to garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shu of Lüeyang, connected by marriage to Yang Jun, intrigued to supplant Long, claiming he was senile and unfit for command; the court recalled Long and installed Shu.

sentences.zh: 氏、羌聚結，百姓驚懼。

translations.literal: The Di and Qiang gathered and banded together; the hundred surnames were frightened and fearful.
translations.idiomatic: Di and Qiang tribes rose together and the populace panicked.

sentences.zh: 朝廷恐關隴復擾，乃免舒，遣隆復職，竟卒於官。

translations.literal: The court feared Guan and Long would again be disturbed; thereupon it dismissed Shu and sent Long back to office; he finally died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing renewed turmoil in Guanzhong and Longyou, the court removed Shu and restored Long, who died in harness.

sentences.zh: 子咸嗣，亦驍勇。

translations.literal: His son Xian succeeded; he too was fierce and brave.
translations.idiomatic: His heir Xian inherited his fierceness in battle.

sentences.zh: 成都王穎攻長沙王乂，以咸為鷹揚將軍，率兵屯河橋中渚，為乂將王瑚所敗，沒於陣。

translations.literal: Prince Chengdu Ying attacked Prince Changsha Yi; he employed Xian as General Who Displays Hawkery, leading troops garrisoned on the mid-islet of the He Bridge; he was defeated by Yi's general Wang Hu and drowned in the ranks.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Chengdu Sima Ying struck Prince Changsha Sima Yi, Xian served as General Who Displays Hawkery on the mid-channel fort at the Yellow River bridge until Yi's general Wang Hu broke him and he fell in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 胡奮

translations.literal: Hu Fen — biography heading.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Fen.

sentences.zh: 胡奮，字玄威，安定臨涇人也，魏車騎將軍陰密侯遵之子也。

translations.literal: Hu Fen, courtesy name Xuanwei, was a native of Linjing in Anding; he was the son of Wei General of Chariots and Cavalry and Marquis of Yinmi Zun.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Fen, courtesy Xuanwei, came from Linjing in Anding—son of Wei General of Chariots and Cavalry and Marquis of Yinmi, Hu Zun.

sentences.zh: 奮性開朗，有籌略，少好武事。

translations.literal: Fen's nature was open and bright; he had stratagem and planning; in youth he loved military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was frank and astute, fond of soldiering even as a young man.

sentences.zh: 宣帝之伐遼東也，以白衣侍從左右，甚見接待。

translations.literal: When the Xuandi campaigned against Liaodong, he attended as a common-clothed attendant at left and right and was greatly received and treated.
translations.idiomatic: During Sima Yi's Liaodong expedition he followed as a civilian attendant and won marked favor.

sentences.zh: 還為校尉，稍遷徐州刺史，封夏陽子。

translations.literal: Returning he became a colonel; gradually promoted to Inspector of Xu Province, enfeoffed as Baron of Xiayang.
translations.idiomatic: Back at court he rose from colonel to Inspector of Xu Province and Baron of Xiayang.

sentences.zh: 匈奴中部帥劉猛叛，使驍騎路蕃討之，以奮為監軍、假節，頓軍硜北，為蕃後繼。

translations.literal: The central commander of the Xiongnu Liu Meng rebelled; he sent Agile Cavalry Lu Fan to strike him; Fen was appointed army supervisor, lent insignia, halted the army north of Jing, as Fan's rear support.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiongnu chief Liu Meng rebelled, swift-cavalry commander Lu Fan was sent against him with Fen as supervising commissioner and rear guard north of Jing.

sentences.zh: 擊猛，破之，猛帳下將李恪斬猛而降。

translations.literal: He attacked Meng, defeated him; Meng's tent officer Li Ke executed Meng and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: He shattered Meng's force, and Meng's own officer Li Ke slew him and capitulated.

sentences.zh: 以功累遷征南將軍、假節、都督荊州諸軍事，遷護軍，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: By merit he was repeatedly promoted General Who Conquers the South, lent insignia, supervised military affairs of Jing Province, promoted to Guards commander, added Cavalier Attendant in Regular Service.
translations.idiomatic: Merit carried him to General Who Conquers the South with acting credentials and command over Jingzhou forces, then guards commander and imperial attendant.

sentences.zh: 奮家世將門，晚乃好學，有刀筆之用，所在有聲績，居邊特有威惠。

translations.literal: Fen's family for generations was a general's gate; in old age he then loved learning; he had the use of brush and knife; wherever he was located he had reputation and traces; dwelling on the border he especially had awe-inspiring kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Though born to a warrior house, he took up scholarship late and proved adept at paperwork; every posting showed results, and on the frontier he combined sternness with generosity.

sentences.zh: 泰始末，武帝怠政事而耽於色，大采擇公卿女以充六宮，奮女選入為貴人。

translations.literal: At the end of Taishi, Emperor Wu slackened government affairs and indulged in sex; he greatly collected and selected daughters of dukes and ministers to fill the six palaces; Fen's daughter was selected and entered as Honored Lady.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Taishi, Emperor Wu neglected statecraft for pleasure and swept noble daughters into the harem; Fen's girl became an Honored Lady.

sentences.zh: 奮唯有一子，為南陽王友，早亡。

translations.literal: Fen had only one son, who was Friend to the Prince of Nanyang and died early.
translations.idiomatic: Fen had but one son, the prince's companion at Nanyang, who died young.

sentences.zh: 及聞女為貴人，哭曰：「老奴不死，唯有二兒，男入九地之下，女上九天之上。

translations.literal: When he heard his daughter had become Honored Lady he wept saying: "This old slave not dying—only having two children—the male has entered beneath the nine earths; the female ascends above the nine heavens."
translations.idiomatic: Learning his daughter had entered the palace he wept: "I should have died sooner—I had only two children: my son lies deep underground while my daughter rises to the clouds."

sentences.zh: 」奮既舊臣，兼有椒房之助，甚見寵待。

translations.literal: " Fen was both an old minister and moreover had pepper-room assistance; he was greatly seen with favor and treatment.
translations.idiomatic: As an elder statesman with an imperial connection through his daughter, he basked in favor.

sentences.zh: 遷左僕射，加鎮軍大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: He was promoted Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, added General Who Stabilizes the Army, Grand Minister of Works, ceremonies equal to the Three Offices.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Left Vice Director, General Who Stabilizes the Army, and minister with ceremonies matching the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 時楊駿以後父驕傲自得，奮謂駿曰：「卿恃女更益豪邪？

translations.literal: At the time Yang Jun because he was empress father was arrogant and self-satisfied; Fen said to Jun: "You rely on your daughter to become still more overbearing?"
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jun swaggered as the empress dowager's father, Fen asked whether his daughter's rank made him bolder still.

sentences.zh: 曆觀前代，與天家婚，未有不滅門者，但早晚事耳。

translations.literal: " Looking through former generations, those who marry the imperial house never avoid extinction of the whole gate—it is only a matter of sooner or later."
translations.idiomatic: "Study history: matches with the imperial clan always end in clan-wide ruin—only the timing varies."

sentences.zh: 觀卿舉措，適所以速禍。

translations.literal: " Observing your movements and measures, they suit exactly what hastens disaster."
translations.idiomatic: "Judging your conduct, you are inviting catastrophe faster every day."

sentences.zh: 」駿曰：「卿女不在天家乎？

translations.literal: " Jun said: "Is not your daughter also not in the imperial house?"
translations.idiomatic: Jun shot back: "Your own daughter lives in the palace too."

sentences.zh: 」奮曰：「我女與卿女作婢耳，何能損益！

translations.literal: " Fen said: "My daughter serves your daughter as a maid—how can she harm or benefit!"
translations.idiomatic: Fen answered: "My girl is little better than your daughter's maid—she hardly shifts the balance."

sentences.zh: 」時人皆為之懼，駿雖銜之，而不能害。

translations.literal: " At the time people all for him were fearful; Jun although harbored resentment toward him could not harm him.
translations.idiomatic: Listeners trembled for Fen; Jun hated him but could not strike.

sentences.zh: 後卒于官，贈車騎將軍，諡曰壯。

translations.literal: Later he died in office; posthumously awarded General of Chariots and Cavalry; posthumous title Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office and was posthumously named General of Chariots and Cavalry with the epithet Zhuang, "the Stalwart."

sentences.zh: 奮兄弟六人，兄廣，弟烈，並知名。

translations.literal: Fen's brothers were six men; elder brother Guang, younger brother Lie; both were known by reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Among six brothers, Guang and Lie were especially celebrated.

sentences.zh: 廣字宣祖，位至散騎常侍、少府。

translations.literal: Guang's courtesy name was Xuanzu; his rank reached Cavalier Attendant in Regular Service and Minister of the Royal Household.
translations.idiomatic: Guang, courtesy Xuanzu, rose to imperial attendant and minister of the royal household.

sentences.zh: 廣子喜，字林甫，亦以開濟為稱，仕至涼州刺史、建武將軍、假節、護羌校尉。

translations.literal: Guang's son Xi, courtesy name Linfu, also by breadth and aid was praised; his office reached Inspector of Liang Province, General Who Establishes Might, lent insignia, Colonel Who Protects the Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: Guang's son Xi, courtesy Linfu, famed for enterprise and generosity, became Inspector of Liang Province, General Who Establishes Might, with Qiang-colonel credentials.

sentences.zh: 烈字武玄，為將伐蜀。

translations.literal: Lie's courtesy name was Wuxuan; he was a general who campaigned against Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Lie, courtesy Wuxuan, had commanded troops against Shu.

sentences.zh: 鐘會之反也，烈與諸將皆被閉。

translations.literal: When Zhong Hui rebelled, Lie with the various generals was all locked up.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhong Hui mutinied, Lie and the other generals were confined.

sentences.zh: 烈子世元，時年十八，為士卒先，攻殺會，名馳遠近。

translations.literal: Lie's son Shiyuan, at that time eighteen years of age, was foremost among the soldiers; he attacked and killed Hui; his name galloped far and near.
translations.idiomatic: Lie's eighteen-year-old son Shiyuan led the stormers who slew Zhong Hui and won fame across the realm.

sentences.zh: 烈為秦州刺史，及涼州叛，烈屯于萬斛堆，為虜所圍，無援，遇害。

translations.literal: Lie was Inspector of Qin Province; when Liang Province rebelled, Lie encamped at Wanhudui; he was surrounded by barbarians, without relief, and met harm.
translations.idiomatic: As Inspector of Qin Province he was trapped at Wanhudui when Liangzhou rose; isolated among tribesmen, he was killed.

sentences.zh: 陶璜

translations.literal: Tao Huang — biography heading.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Huang.

sentences.zh: 陶璜，字世英，丹陽秣陵人也。

translations.literal: Tao Huang, courtesy name Shiying, was a native of Moling in Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Huang, courtesy Shiying, hailed from Moling in Danyang.

sentences.zh: 父基，吳交州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Ji was Wu Inspector of Jiao Province.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tao Ji had been Wu's Inspector of Jiao Province.

sentences.zh: 璜仕吳曆顯位。

translations.literal: Huang served Wu through successive eminent positions.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wu he climbed through high offices.

sentences.zh: 孫皓時，交阯太守孫諝貪暴，為百姓所患。

translations.literal: Under Sun Hao the Administrator of Jiaozhi Sun Xu was greedy and cruel and became what the hundred surnames dreaded.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao's prefect Sun Xu of Jiaozhi governed with greed and cruelty until the people loathed him.

sentences.zh: 會察戰鄧荀至，擅調孔雀三千頭，遣送秣陵，既苦遠役，咸思為亂。

translations.literal: When the inspector-at-war Deng Gou arrived, he arbitrarily conscripted three thousand peacocks to dispatch to Moling; already suffering bitter distant labor, all thought to rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector Deng Gou then demanded three thousand peacock feathers shipped to the capital; the crushing levy drove everyone toward revolt.

sentences.zh: 郡吏呂興殺諝及荀，以郡內附。

translations.literal: County clerk Lu Xing killed Xu and Gou and with the commandery attached inward.
translations.idiomatic: County clerk Lu Xing assassinated Xu and Gou and brought the prefecture over to Jin.

sentences.zh: 武帝拜興安南將軍、交阯太守。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu appointed Xing General Who Pacifies the South and Administrator of Jiaozhi.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu named Lu Xing General Who Pacifies the South and prefect of Jiaozhi.

sentences.zh: 尋為其功曹李統所殺，帝更以建甯爨穀為交阯太守，谷又死，更遣巴西馬融代之。

translations.literal: Soon he was killed by his merit clerk Li Tong; the Emperor replaced him with Jianning Cuan Gu as Administrator of Jiaozhi; Gu also died; again they sent Ba's Ma Rong to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xing soon fell to his aide Li Tong; the court replaced him with Cuan Gu of Jianning, then Ba's Ma Rong after Gu died.

sentences.zh: 融病卒，南中監軍霍弋又遣犍為楊稷代融，與將軍毛炅，九真太守董元，牙門孟幹、孟通、李松、王業、爨能等，自蜀出交阯，破吳軍於古城，斬大都督修則、交州刺史劉俊。

translations.literal: Rong died of illness; southern inspector Huo Yi again sent Qianwei Yang Ji to replace Rong, with general Mao Jiong, Jiuzhen Administrator Dong Yuan, Ya Gate officers Meng Gan, Meng Tong, Li Song, Wang Ye, Cuan Neng and others, emerging from Shu to Jiaozhi; they defeated Wu troops at Gucheng, executed Grand Commander Xiu Ze and Inspector Liu Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Rong died in office; Huo Yi sent Yang Ji from Qianwei with Mao Jiong, Dong Yuan of Jiuzhen, and gate officers Meng Gan, Meng Tong, Li Song, Wang Ye, and Cuan Neng. They struck from Shu into Jiaozhi, routed Wu at Gucheng, and killed commander Xiu Ze and Inspector Liu Jun.

sentences.zh: 吳遣虞汜為監軍，薛珝為威南將軍、大都督，璜為蒼梧太守，距稷，戰于分水。

translations.literal: Wu sent Yu Si as inspector-at-war, Xue Xu as General Who Displays Might in the South and grand commander, Huang as Administrator of Cangwu, resisting Ji; they fought at Fenshui.
translations.idiomatic: Wu countered with Yu Si as army overseer, Xue Xu as southern commander, and Tao Huang as Cangwu prefect to oppose Yang Ji at Fenshui.

sentences.zh: 璜敗，退保合浦，亡其二將。

translations.literal: Huang was defeated, withdrew to defend Hepu, and lost two of his generals.
translations.idiomatic: Huang lost and fell back to Hepu, forfeiting two generals.

sentences.zh: 珝怒謂璜曰：「若自表討賊，而喪二帥，其責安在？

translations.literal: Xu angrily said to Huang: "If you yourself memorialized to attack the bandits yet lost two commanders—where lies the blame?"
translations.idiomatic: Xue Xu demanded how Tao Huang could petition for the campaign yet lose two leaders.

sentences.zh: 」璜曰：「下官不得行意，諸軍不相順，故致敗耳。

translations.literal: " Huang said: "Your inferior official could not exercise his intent; the various armies did not obey each other—therefore defeat occurred."
translations.idiomatic: Huang answered that rival officers ignored him and coordination collapsed.

sentences.zh: 」珝怒，欲引軍還。

translations.literal: " Xu was angry and wished to lead the army back.
translations.idiomatic: Furious, Xu prepared to withdraw the army.

sentences.zh: 璜夜以數百兵襲董元，獲其寶物，船載而歸，珝乃謝之，以璜領交州，為前部督。

translations.literal: Huang by night with several hundred troops raided Dong Yuan, seized his treasures, loaded them on boats and returned; Xu then apologized to him, put Huang in charge of Jiao Province, as forward commander.
translations.idiomatic: Huang salvaged the situation with a night raid on Dong Yuan's stockpiles, floated the loot back, apologized to Xu, regained command as Jiaozhou's forward director.

sentences.zh: 璜從海道出於不意，徑至交阯，元距之。

translations.literal: Huang exited by sea route from outside expectation, went straight to Jiaozhi; Yuan resisted him.
translations.idiomatic: He then surprised the enemy with a seaward thrust straight at Jiaozhi, where Dong Yuan blocked him.

sentences.zh: 諸將將戰，璜疑斷牆內有伏兵，列長戟於甚後。

translations.literal: When the generals were about to fight, Huang suspected broken walls inside held ambush troops; he lined long halberds behind him.
translations.idiomatic: Suspecting ambush inside the ruined walls, he kept halberdiers to his rear.

sentences.zh: 兵才接，元偽退，璜追之，伏兵果出，長戟逆之，大破元等。

translations.literal: When troops had just engaged, Yuan feigned retreat; Huang pursued him; ambush troops indeed emerged; long halberds opposed them; they greatly defeated Yuan and others.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan feigned flight; Huang chased him into an ambush, but his rear halberds wheeled and shattered Yuan's trap.

sentences.zh: 以前所得寶船上錦物數千匹遺扶嚴賊帥梁奇，奇將萬餘人助璜。

translations.literal: He took brocade goods several thousand bolts from what was obtained earlier on treasure boats and presented them to Fuyan bandit chief Liang Qi; Qi led more than ten thousand men to assist Huang.
translations.idiomatic: He bribed Fuyan warlord Liang Qi with thousands of bolts of silk captured earlier, and Qi brought ten thousand warriors to Huang's aid.

sentences.zh: 元有勇將解系同在城內，璜誘其弟象，使為書與系，又使象乘璜軺車，鼓吹導從而行。

translations.literal: Yuan had a fierce general Xie Xi together inside the city; Huang enticed his younger brother Xiang, made him write to Xi, and also made Xiang ride Huang's light carriage with drum band escort proceeding.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan's champion Xie Xi held the citadel; Huang coaxed Xi's brother Xiang into forging letters and paraded Xiang in Tao Huang's carriage behind musicians.

sentences.zh: 元等曰：「象尚若此，系必去志。

translations.literal: " Yuan and others said: "If Xiang is already like this, Xi is certain to have the intent to leave."
translations.idiomatic: The defenders decided that if Xiang had switched sides, Xi would desert too.

sentences.zh: 」乃就殺之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon they went and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: They executed Xi on that suspicion.

sentences.zh: 珝、璜遂陷交阯。

translations.literal: Xu and Huang thereupon captured Jiaozhi.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Xu and Tao Huang then took Jiaozhi.

sentences.zh: 吳因用璜為交州刺史。

translations.literal: Wu thereupon employed Huang as Inspector of Jiao Province.
translations.idiomatic: Wu appointed Tao Huang Inspector of Jiao Province.

sentences.zh: 璜有謀策，周窮好施，能得人心。

translations.literal: Huang had stratagems and plans, was thorough in poverty and fond of giving, and was able to win people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Huang was a shrewd planner, generous to the poor, and won deep loyalty.

sentences.zh: 滕修數討南賊，不能制，璜曰：「南岸仰吾鹽鐵，斷勿與市，皆壞為田器。

translations.literal: Teng Xiu several times campaigned against the southern bandits and could not control them; Huang said: "The south bank relies on our salt and iron; cut off and do not market to them—they will all break and make field tools."
translations.idiomatic: When Teng Xiu could not subdue the south, Huang advised choking their supply of salt and iron until their metal tools became plowshares.

sentences.zh: 如此二年，可一戰而滅也。

translations.literal: " In this way two years, one battle can annihilate them."
translations.idiomatic: "In two years of that embargo you can finish them in a single action."

sentences.zh: 」修從之，果破賊。

translations.literal: " Xiu followed him and indeed broke the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu followed the advice and crushed the rebels.

sentences.zh: 初，霍弋之遣稷、炅等，與之誓曰：「若賊圍城未百日而降者，家屬誅；

translations.literal: Earlier, when Huo Yi dispatched Ji, Jiong and others, he swore with them: "If the bandits besiege the city and before one hundred days you surrender, households will be executed."
translations.idiomatic: Before dispatching Yang Ji and Mao Jiong, Huo Yi had sworn: surrender within the hundred-day siege and your families die.

sentences.zh: 若過百日救兵不至，吾受其罪。

translations.literal: " If past one hundred days relief troops do not arrive, I will bear the blame."
translations.idiomatic: "Hold past one hundred days without relief and I alone accept punishment."

sentences.zh: 」稷等守未百日，糧盡，乞降，璜不許，給其糧使守。

translations.literal: " Ji and others defended not yet one hundred days; provisions were exhausted; they begged to surrender; Huang did not permit; he supplied them grain and made them defend.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Ji gave up before the hundredth day when food ran out; Huang refused surrender but sent grain so they could keep fighting.

sentences.zh: 諸將並諫，璜曰：「霍弋已死，不能救稷等必矣，可須其日滿，然後受降，使彼得無罪，我受有義，內訓百姓，外懷鄰國，不亦可乎！

translations.literal: " The various generals together remonstrated; Huang said: "Huo Yi is already dead; he cannot save Ji and others—it is certain; one can wait until their day is full, then accept surrender, letting them obtain guiltlessness and our receiving righteousness; inwardly instructing the hundred surnames, outwardly cherishing neighboring states—is it not also allowable!"
translations.idiomatic: His officers protested, but Huang argued: "Huo Yi is dead and cannot rescue them—wait until the sworn term ends, then accept surrender so the garrison keeps honor and Jin keeps faith with neighbors and subjects alike."

sentences.zh: 」稷等期訖糧盡，救兵不至，乃納之。

translations.literal: " When Ji and others' term ended provisions were exhausted and relief did not arrive, then he admitted them.
translations.idiomatic: When the deadline passed and supplies failed with no reinforcements, he took their surrender.

sentences.zh: 修則既為毛炅所殺，則子允隨璜南征，城既降，允求復仇，璜不許。

translations.literal: Xiu Ze had already been killed by Mao Jiong; Ze's son Yun followed Huang on the southern campaign; when the city had surrendered Yun sought revenge; Huang did not permit.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu Ze had died at Mao Jiong's hands; Ze's son Yun marched south with Huang and, after the city fell, demanded vengeance—Huang refused.

sentences.zh: 炅密謀襲璜，事覺，收炅，呵曰：「晉賊！

translations.literal: Jiong secretly plotted to raid Huang; the affair was discovered; they seized Jiong; he shouted: "Jin bandit!"
translations.idiomatic: Mao Jiong plotted to ambush Huang, was seized, and screamed "Jin dogs!"

sentences.zh: 」炅厲聲曰：「吳狗！

translations.literal: " Jiong in stern voice said: "Wu dog!"
translations.idiomatic: Mao Jiong shot back: "Wu cur!"

sentences.zh: 何等為賊？

translations.literal: " What counts as bandit?"
translations.idiomatic: "Who are the real bandits here?"

sentences.zh: 」允剖其腹，曰：「復能作賊不？

translations.literal: " Yun split open his belly and said: "Can you still make banditry?"
translations.idiomatic: Yun disemboweled him, jeering, "Still feel like rebelling?"

sentences.zh: 」炅猶罵曰：「吾志殺汝孫皓，汝父何死狗也！

translations.literal: " Jiong still cursed saying: "My intent was to kill your Sun Hao—what kind of dead dog is your father!"
translations.idiomatic: Jiong kept shouting that his aim had been Sun Hao's head—what sort of dead cur was Yun's father anyway!

sentences.zh: 」璜既擒稷等，並送之。

translations.literal: " When Huang had captured Ji and others, he sent them all together.
translations.idiomatic: Huang sent his prisoners, including Yang Ji, on under escort.

sentences.zh: 稷至合浦，發病死。

translations.literal: When Ji reached Hepu, he developed illness and died.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Ji fell ill at Hepu and died.

sentences.zh: 孟幹、爨能、李松等至建鄴，皓將殺之。

translations.literal: Meng Gan, Cuan Neng, Li Song and others reached Jianye; Hao was about to execute them.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Gan, Cuan Neng, and Li Song reached Jianye, where Sun Hao meant to put them to death.

sentences.zh: 或勸皓，幹等忠於所事，宜宥之以勸邊將，皓從其言，將徙之臨海。

translations.literal: Some urged Hao that Gan and others were loyal to what they served; it was fitting to forgive them to encourage border generals; Hao followed their words and was about to relocate them to Linhai.
translations.idiomatic: Advisers argued that their loyalty deserved mercy and would encourage frontier commanders; Sun Hao agreed and planned to exile them to Linhai.

sentences.zh: 幹等志欲北歸，慮東徙轉遠，以吳人愛蜀側竹弩，言能作之，皓留付作部。

translations.literal: Gan and others intended to return north and worried eastern relocation would grow ever farther; because Wu people prized Shu-style bamboo crossbows, they claimed they could make them; Hao retained them and handed them to the workshop bureau.
translations.idiomatic: They wanted to escape north and dreaded being sent farther east, so they claimed they could craft the Shu bamboo crossbows Wu prized; Hao kept them in the imperial workshops.

sentences.zh: 後幹逃至京都，松、能為皓所殺。

translations.literal: Later Gan fled to the capital; Song and Neng were killed by Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Gan later fled to Luoyang; Sun Hao executed Song and Neng.

sentences.zh: 幹陳伐吳之計，帝乃厚加賞賜，以為日南太守。

translations.literal: Gan submitted plans for attacking Wu; the Emperor then richly rewarded him and appointed him Administrator of Rinan.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Gan presented a strategy for conquering Wu; the court rewarded him handsomely and named him prefect of Rinan.

sentences.zh: 先是，以楊稷為交州刺史，毛炅為交阯太守，印緩未至而敗，即贈稷交州，炅及松能子並關內侯。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yang Ji had been appointed Inspector of Jiao Province and Mao Jiong Administrator of Jiaozhi; seals and ribbons had not arrived before defeat; posthumously Ji was invested Inspector of Jiao Province, and Jiong together with Song and Neng's sons were all granted secondary marquis within the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Ji and Mao Jiong had already been named to Jiao Province and Jiaozhi before their seals arrived; posthumously Ji received full inspector honors, while Jiong plus Song's and Neng's sons each gained secondary marquis titles.

sentences.zh: 九真郡功曹李祚保郡內附，璜遣將攻之，不克。

translations.literal: Jiuzhen merit clerk Li Zuo held the commandery and attached inward; Huang dispatched generals to attack him and did not conquer.
translations.idiomatic: Jiuzhen clerk Li Zuo held out for Jin; Tao Huang attacked him unsuccessfully.

sentences.zh: 祚舅黎晃隨軍。

translations.literal: Zuo's maternal uncle Li Huang followed the army.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo's uncle Li Huang rode with Huang's army.

sentences.zh: 勸祚令降。

translations.literal: He urged Zuo to order surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Huang urged Li Zuo to yield.

sentences.zh: 祚答曰：「舅自吳將，祚自晉臣，唯力是視耳。

translations.literal: Zuo replied: "Uncle, you are yourself a Wu general; I am myself a Jin subject—only strength is looked to."
translations.idiomatic: Zuo answered: "You fight for Wu; I serve Jin—may the stronger win."

sentences.zh: 」逾時乃拔。

translations.literal: " After extended time he then took it.
translations.idiomatic: After a prolonged siege Tao Huang finally captured the city.

sentences.zh: 皓以璜為使持節、都督交州諸軍事、前將軍、交州牧。

translations.literal: Hao appointed Huang Bearer of the Credential and Staff, supervised military affairs of Jiao Province, Forward General, and Shepherd of Jiao Province.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao named Tao Huang commander of Jiao forces with full powers, Forward General, and governor.

sentences.zh: 武平、九德、新昌土地阻險，夷獠勁悍，曆世不賓，璜征討，開置三郡，及九真屬國三十餘縣。

translations.literal: Wuping, Jiude, and Xinchang lands were obstructed and perilous; Yi and Liao were stalwart and fierce; through generations they had not submitted; Huang campaigned and opened and established three commanderies, and Jiuzhen dependent state more than thirty counties.
translations.idiomatic: Wuping, Jiude, and Xinchang were rugged country of fierce tribal peoples who had never paid tribute; Huang conquered them, carved out three new commands, and annexed thirty-odd counties under Jiuzhen dependency.

sentences.zh: 征璜為武昌都督，以合浦太守修允代之。

translations.literal: Huang was summoned as supervisor of Wuchang; Administrator of Hepu Xiu Yun replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: The court recalled Tao Huang to command at Wuchang and installed Xiu Yun of Hepu in his place.

sentences.zh: 交土人請留璜以千數，於是遣還。

translations.literal: Jiao lands people requested to retain Huang by the thousands; thereupon he was dispatched back.
translations.idiomatic: Thousands of Jiao residents petitioned to keep him, so he was sent back south.

sentences.zh: 皓既降晉，手書遣璜息融敕璜歸順。

translations.literal: When Hao had already surrendered to Jin, he handwrote an order to Huang's son Rong instructing Huang to submit.
translations.idiomatic: After capitulating, Sun Hao wrote personally to Huang's son Tao Rong ordering Huang to submit to Jin.

sentences.zh: 璜流涕數日，遣使送印綬詣洛陽。

translations.literal: Huang wept flowing tears several days; he dispatched envoys sending seals and ribbons to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Huang wept for days, then forwarded his seals to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 帝詔復其本職，封宛陵侯，改為冠軍將軍。

translations.literal: The Emperor's edict restored his original office, enfeoffed him Marquis of Wanling, changed to General Who Champions the Army.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor restored his former post, enfeoffed him as Marquis of Wanling, and redesignated him General Who Champions the Army.

sentences.zh: 吳既平，普減州郡兵，璜上言曰：

translations.literal: After Wu was pacified, generally province and commandery troops were reduced; Huang submitted words saying:
translations.idiomatic: When Wu fell and garrisons were cut, Tao Huang memorialized:

sentences.zh: 又以「合浦郡土地磽確，無有田農，百姓唯以采珠為業，商賈去來，以珠貿米。

translations.literal: Further with "Hepu commandery land is barren stony soil; there are no field farms; the hundred surnames rely solely on gathering pearls for livelihood; merchants come and go, trading pearls for rice."
translations.idiomatic: He noted that barren Hepu depended on pearl diving—farmers traded pearls for grain.

sentences.zh: 而吳時珠禁甚嚴，慮百姓私散好珠，禁絕來去，人以饑困。

translations.literal: " Yet under Wu pearl prohibitions were very strict; fearing commoners would privately scatter fine pearls, they cut off coming and going; people thereby suffered hunger and distress."
translations.idiomatic: Wu had banned exports so fiercely that commerce halted and people starved.

sentences.zh: 又所調猥多，限每不充。

translations.literal: " Moreover what was levied was excessively much; quotas each time were not filled."
translations.idiomatic: Tax quotas were crushing and never met.

sentences.zh: 今請上珠三分輸二，次者輸一，粗者蠲除。

translations.literal: " Now I request top-grade pearls remit two parts in three, middling remit one part, coarse be remitted entirely."
translations.idiomatic: He proposed remitting two-thirds of fine pearls, half of middling grades, and exempting coarse ones.

sentences.zh: 自十月訖二月，非采上珠之時，聽商旅往來如舊」。

translations.literal: " From tenth month through second month is not the season for gathering top pearls; listen to merchants and travelers coming and going as of old."
translations.idiomatic: Between the tenth and second months—the off-season for prime pearls—trade should flow freely again.

sentences.zh: 並從之。

translations.literal: And both followed him.
translations.idiomatic: The throne accepted every item.

sentences.zh: 在南三十年，威恩著於殊俗。

translations.literal: In the south thirty years, awe and kindness showed on alien customs.
translations.idiomatic: For thirty years his kindness and authority shaped distant peoples.

sentences.zh: 及卒，舉州號哭，如喪慈親。

translations.literal: When he died, the whole province wailed and cried as if mourning a kind parent.
translations.idiomatic: When he died the province mourned like bereaved children.

sentences.zh: 朝廷乃以員外散騎常侍吾彥代璜。

translations.literal: The court thereupon used Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant in Regular Service Wu Yan to replace Huang.
translations.idiomatic: The court named Wu Yan supernumerary attendant to succeed him.

sentences.zh: 彥卒，又以員外散騎常侍顧秘代彥。

translations.literal: When Yan died, again used Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant in Regular Service Gu Mi to replace Yan.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Yan died, Gu Mi replaced him in the same capacity.

sentences.zh: 秘卒，州人逼秘子參領州事。

translations.literal: When Mi died, provincials pressed Mi's son Shen to lead provincial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After Gu Mi died locals pressed his son Gu Shen to govern.

sentences.zh: 參尋卒，參弟壽求領州，州人不聽，固求之，遂領州。

translations.literal: Shen soon died; Shen's younger brother Shou sought to lead the province; provincials did not listen; he firmly sought it; thereupon he led the province.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Shen died quickly; brother Gu Shou seized power despite popular opposition.

sentences.zh: 壽乃殺長史胡肇等，又將殺帳下督梁碩，碩走得免，起兵討壽，禽之，會壽母，令鴆殺之。

translations.literal: Shou then killed Senior Clerk Hu Zhao and others, and also was about to kill tent supervisor Liang Shuo; Shuo fled and escaped; he raised troops to attack Shou, seized him; encountering Shou's mother, ordered her to poison-kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Shou murdered registrar Hu Zhao and meant to kill aide Liang Shuo, who escaped, rallied troops, captured Shuo, and forced Shou's mother to poison her son.

sentences.zh: 碩乃迎璜子蒼梧太守威領刺史，在職甚得百姓心，三年卒。

translations.literal: Shuo then welcomed Huang's son Administrator of Cangwu Wei to lead inspector; in office he greatly obtained the hundred surnames' hearts; he died in three years.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Shuo then invited Tao Huang's son Tao Wei, prefect of Cangwu, to serve as inspector; Tao Wei won the people in three years before dying.

sentences.zh: 威弟淑，子綏，後並為交州。

translations.literal: Wei's younger brother Shu, son Sui—later both became Jiao Province.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's brother Shu and son Sui later held Jiao Province as well.

sentences.zh: 自基至綏四世，為交州者五人。

translations.literal: From Ji to Sui four generations; those who were Jiao Province were five men.
translations.idiomatic: Four generations from Tao Ji to Tao Sui produced five inspectors of Jiao.

sentences.zh: 璜弟-{濬}-，吳鎮南大將軍、荊州牧。

translations.literal: Huang's younger brother Jun was Wu General Who Guards the South and Inspector of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Huang's brother Tao Jun had been Wu's southern commander and Jingzhou inspector.

sentences.zh: -{濬}-弟抗，太子中庶子。

translations.literal: Jun's younger brother Kang was Palace Attendant to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Jun's brother Tao Kang served the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: -{濬}-子湮，字恭之；

translations.literal: Jun's son Yan, courtesy name Gongzhi;
translations.idiomatic: Tao Jun's son Tao Yan, courtesy Gongzhi;

sentences.zh: 湮弟猷，字恭豫，並有名。

translations.literal: Yan's younger brother You, courtesy name Gongyu—both had reputation.
translations.idiomatic: his brother Tao You, courtesy Gongyu—both were celebrated.

sentences.zh: 湮至臨海太守、黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: Yan reached Administrator of Linhai and Palace Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Yan rose to prefect of Linhai and palace gentleman.

sentences.zh: 猷宣城內史，王導右軍長史。

translations.literal: You was interior steward of Xuancheng and chief clerk on Wang Dao's right army.
translations.idiomatic: Tao You governed Xuancheng interiorly and served Wang Dao as chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 湮子馥，於湖令，為韓晃所殺，追贈廬江太守。

translations.literal: Yan's son Fu was magistrate of Wuhu and was killed by Han Huang; posthumously invested Administrator of Lujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Fu, magistrate of Wuhu, died at Han Huang's hands and was posthumously named prefect of Lujiang.

sentences.zh: 抗子回，自有傳。

translations.literal: Kang's son Hui has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kang's son Tao Hui has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 吾彥

translations.literal: Wu Yan — biography heading.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yan.

sentences.zh: 吾彥，字士則，吳郡吳人也。

translations.literal: Wu Yan, courtesy name Shize, was a native of Wu in Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yan, courtesy Shize, came from Wu county.

sentences.zh: 出自寒微，有文武才幹。

translations.literal: He emerged from cold and lowly background; he had civil and military talent and capacity.
translations.idiomatic: Of humble birth, he possessed both literary and martial gifts.

sentences.zh: 身長八尺，手格猛獸，旅力絕群。

translations.literal: His body was eight chi tall; with hands he grappled fierce beasts; traveling strength cut off the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: He stood eight chi tall, wrestled beasts barehanded, and had uncommon strength.

sentences.zh: 仕吳為通江吏。

translations.literal: He served Wu as Tong River clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wu he worked as a Yangtze patrol clerk.

sentences.zh: 時將軍薛珝杖節南征，軍容甚盛，彥觀之，慨然而歎。

translations.literal: At the time General Xue Xu bore insignia on southern campaign; military appearance was very magnificent; Yan watched it and sighed with emotion.
translations.idiomatic: Watching Xue Xu's splendid southern expedition, he sighed with longing.

sentences.zh: 有善相者劉劄謂之曰：「以君之相，後當至此，不足慕也。

translations.literal: There was a skilled physiognomist Liu Zha who said to him: "Judging by your physiognomy, later you ought to reach this—it is not worth admiring."
translations.idiomatic: The physiognomist Liu Zha told him his face promised equal rank someday.

sentences.zh: 」初為小將，給吳大司馬陸抗。

translations.literal: " First he was a minor officer, assigned to Wu Grand Marshal Lu Kang.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a junior aide to Grand Marshal Lu Kang.

sentences.zh: 抗奇其勇略，將拔用之，患眾情不允，乃會諸將，密使人陽狂拔刀跳躍而來，坐上諸將皆懼而走，唯彥不動，舉幾禦之，眾服其勇，乃擢用焉。

translations.literal: Kang marveled at his courage and planning and wished to promote him but worried crowd feeling would not consent; thereupon he assembled the various generals, secretly sent a man to feign madness, draw a sword, leap and come; seated generals all were frightened and fled—only Yan did not move, raised a bench to ward him off; the multitude admired his courage; thereupon he was promoted and employed.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Kang prized his valor but feared resentment; at a banquet he staged a fake assassin; officers fled while Wu Yan held his seat and blocked the blade with a stool—proving his nerve and earning promotion.

sentences.zh: 稍遷建平太守。

translations.literal: Gradually promoted Administrator of Jianping.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to prefect of Jianping.

sentences.zh: 時王濬將伐吳，造船於蜀，彥覺之，請增兵為備，皓不從，彥乃輒為鐵鎖，橫斷江路。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Jun was about to attack Wu and built ships in Shu; Yan perceived it and requested to increase troops for preparation; Hao did not follow; Yan then on his own authority made iron chains, horizontally cutting off the Yangtze route.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Jun built warships in Shu, Wu Yan asked Sun Hao for reinforcements; refused, he stretched iron chains across the river himself.

sentences.zh: 及師臨境，緣江諸城皆望風降附，或見攻而拔，唯彥堅守，大眾攻之不能克，乃退舍禮之。

translations.literal: When the army reached the border, along the Yangtze various cities all lowered wind and surrendered or attached, or were seen attacked and taken; only Yan firmly defended; the great host attacked him and could not conquer; thereupon withdrew camp and treated him with courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: As Jin swept downstream, cities surrendered—only Wu Yan held until besiegers withdrew and honored him.

sentences.zh: 吳亡，彥始歸降，武帝以為金城太守。

translations.literal: Wu perished; Yan first submitted to surrender; Emperor Wu appointed him Administrator of Jincheng.
