translations.idiomatic: After Wu fell he capitulated and Emperor Wu named him prefect of Jincheng.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗從容問薛瑩曰：「孫皓所以亡國者何也？

translations.literal: The Emperor once leisurely asked Xue Ying: "For what reason did Sun Hao lose the state?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu once asked Xue Ying why Sun Hao fell.

sentences.zh: 」瑩對曰：「歸命侯臣皓之君吳，昵近小人，刑罰妄加，大臣大將無所親信，人人憂恐，各不自安，敗亡之釁，由此而作矣。

translations.literal: " Ying replied: "The Submit-to-Destiny Marquis subject Hao's ruling Wu favored petty men; punishments were recklessly applied; great ministers and great generals had none trusted; every man worried and feared; each did not rest secure; the flaw of defeat and destruction arose from this."
translations.idiomatic: Ying blamed Sun Hao's cruelty, favoritism, and suspicion of his generals.

sentences.zh: 」其後帝又問彥，對曰：「吳主英俊，宰輔賢明。

translations.literal: " Later the Emperor again asked Yan; he replied: "The Wu lord was handsome and talented; chief ministers were worthy and bright."
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yan answered that Sun Hao was brilliant and his ministers wise.

sentences.zh: 」帝笑曰：「君明臣賢，何為亡國？

translations.literal: " The Emperor laughed saying: "If lord is bright and ministers worthy, why lose the state?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed: wise ruler and good ministers—how lose a realm?

sentences.zh: 」彥曰：「天祿永終，歷數有屬，所以為陛下擒。

translations.literal: " Yan said: "Heaven's salary ends forever; the succession has its assignee—therefore he became Your Majesty's captive."
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yan answered that Heaven had transferred the mandate, hence Sun Hao became a captive.

sentences.zh: 此蓋天時，豈人事也！

translations.literal: " This is covered by Heaven's timing—how could it be human affairs!"
translations.idiomatic: Heaven decreed it, not human error.

sentences.zh: 」張華時在坐，謂彥曰：「君為吳將，積有歲年，蔑爾無聞，竊所惑矣。

translations.literal: " Zhang Hua at the time was seated; he said to Yan: "You were a Wu general; accumulating years you were obscurely without fame—I privately am puzzled."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua muttered that a veteran Wu commander should not have been unknown.

sentences.zh: 」彥厲聲曰：「陛下知我，而卿不聞乎？

translations.literal: " Yan in stern voice said: "Your Majesty knows me—yet you have not heard?"
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yan snapped that the emperor knew him even if Zhang Hua did not.

sentences.zh: 」帝甚嘉之。」

translations.literal: " The Emperor greatly praised him."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu applauded the retort.

sentences.zh: 轉在敦煌，威恩甚著。

translations.literal: Transferred to Dunhuang; awe and kindness were greatly manifest.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Dunhuang, he governed with renown.

sentences.zh: 遷雁門太守。

translations.literal: Promoted Administrator of Yanmen.
translations.idiomatic: He became prefect of Yanmen.

sentences.zh: 時順陽王暢驕縱，前後內史皆誣之以罪。

translations.literal: At the time Prince of Shunyang Chang was arrogant and unrestrained; former interior stewards all falsely accused him with crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Sima Chang of Shunyang was violent; earlier prefects framed him to survive.

sentences.zh: 乃彥為順陽內史，彥清身率下，威刑嚴肅，眾皆畏懼。

translations.literal: When Yan became interior steward of Shunyang, Yan cleared himself and led subordinates; awe and punishments were severe and solemn; the multitude all feared and dreaded.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yan ruled sternly and cleanly, frightening prince and people alike.

sentences.zh: 暢不能誣，乃更薦之，冀其去職。

translations.literal: Chang could not falsely accuse; then again recommended him, hoping he would leave office.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to fabricate charges, the prince recommended Wu Yan upward hoping to oust him.

sentences.zh: 遷員外散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Promoted Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant in Regular Service.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to supernumerary imperial attendant.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗問彥：「陸喜、陸抗二人誰多也？

translations.literal: The Emperor once asked Yan: "Between Lu Xi and Lu Kang, who was greater?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu asked whether Lu Xi or Lu Kang was superior.

sentences.zh: 」彥對曰：「道德名望，抗不及喜；

translations.literal: " Yan replied: "In virtue and moral fame Kang did not match Xi;
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yan said Xi surpassed Kang in moral stature.

sentences.zh: 立功立事，喜不及抗。」

translations.literal: " in establishing merit and affairs Xi did not match Kang."
translations.idiomatic: Yet Kang exceeded Xi in battlefield achievements.

sentences.zh: 會交州刺史陶璜卒，以彥為南中都督、交州刺史。

translations.literal: When Inspector of Jiao Province Tao Huang died, Yan was appointed Supervisor of the South Center and Inspector of Jiao Province.
translations.idiomatic: On Tao Huang's death Wu Yan became southern commander and inspector of Jiao.

sentences.zh: 重餉陸機兄弟，機將受之，雲曰：「彥本微賤，為先公所拔，而答詔不善，安可愛之！

translations.literal: He heavily gifted Lu Ji's brothers; Ji was about to accept; Yun said: "Yan originally was mean and lowly, picked up by our late father—yet his reply edict was not good—how can we accept his gifts!"
translations.idiomatic: He sent rich gifts to Lu Ji and Lu Yun; Yun refused because Wu Yan's memorial wording slighted their father.

sentences.zh: 」機乃止。

translations.literal: " Ji thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ji yielded to his brother.

sentences.zh: 因此每毀之。

translations.literal: Because of this each time he slandered him.
translations.idiomatic: The Lu brothers then vilified Wu Yan.

sentences.zh: 長沙孝廉尹虞謂機等曰：「自古由賤而興者，乃有帝王，何但公卿。

translations.literal: Changsha Filially Incorrupt Yin Yu spoke to Ji and others: "From ancient times those who rose from lowliness include even emperors—not only dukes and ministers."
translations.idiomatic: Yin Yu reminded them that humble origins had produced emperors as well as ministers.

sentences.zh: 若何元幹、侯孝明、唐儒宗、張義允等，並起自寒役，皆內侍外鎮，人無譏者。

translations.literal: " If He Yuanqian, Hou Xiaoming, Tang Ruzong, Zhang Yiyun and others all rose from cold labor—all served inside and guarded outside—with none ridiculing them."
translations.idiomatic: He cited risen men like He Yuanqian who commanded armies despite low birth.

sentences.zh: 卿以士則答詔小有不善，毀之無已，吾恐南人皆將去卿，卿便獨坐也。

translations.literal: " You because Shize's reply edict had slight impropriety endlessly slander him—I fear southern men all will leave you and you will sit alone."
translations.idiomatic: Mocking Wu Yan's prose would alienate every southern gentleman.

sentences.zh: 」於是機等意始解，毀言漸息矣。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Ji and others' intention began to resolve; slanderous words gradually ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The Lu brothers relented and gossip faded.

sentences.zh: 初，陶璜之死也，九真戍兵作亂，逐其太守，九真賊帥趙祉圍郡城，彥悉討平之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Tao Huang died, Jiuzhen garrison troops made chaos and expelled their prefect; Jiuzhen bandit chief Zhao Zhi besieged the commandery city; Yan altogether attacked and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: After Tao Huang died, Jiuzhen mutinied and Zhao Zhi besieged the seat until Wu Yan suppressed them.

sentences.zh: 在鎮二十餘年，威恩宣著，南州寧靖。

translations.literal: At post more than twenty years; awe and kindness proclaimed manifest; southern provinces were tranquil and quiet.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty years in command brought calm and gratitude across the south.

sentences.zh: 自表求代，徵為大長秋。

translations.literal: He personally memorialized seeking replacement; summoned as Grand Chamberlain.
translations.idiomatic: He requested relief and was recalled as Grand Chamberlain.

sentences.zh: 卒於官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in harness.

sentences.zh: 張光

translations.literal: Zhang Guang — biography heading.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guang.

sentences.zh: 張光，字景武，江夏鐘武人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Guang, courtesy name Jingwu, was a native of Zhongwu in Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guang, courtesy Jingwu, hailed from Zhongwu in Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 身長八尺，明眉目，美音聲。

translations.literal: His body was eight chi tall; eyes and eyebrows bright; voice and sound beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: Eight chi tall, handsome in face and voice.

sentences.zh: 少為郡吏，家世有部曲，以牙門將伐吳有功，遷江夏西部都尉，轉北地都尉。

translations.literal: In youth he was a commandery clerk; his family generation had personal troops; as Ya Gate general campaigning against Wu he had merit; promoted Western Metropolitan Commandant of Jiangxia; transferred Metropolitan Commandant of Beidi.
translations.idiomatic: A county clerk with family retainers, he earned merit as a gate general against Wu and rose to Jiangxia west commandant, then Beidi commandant.

sentences.zh: 初，趙王倫為關中都督，氐、羌反叛，太守張損戰沒，郡縣吏士少有全者。

translations.literal: Earlier, Prince Zhao Lun was Guanzhong supervisor; Di and Qiang rebelled; Administrator Zhang Sun was killed in battle; commandery and county clerks and soldiers few were preserved whole.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Lun governed Guanzhong, Di and Qiang revolted and prefect Zhang Sun fell; few officers survived.

sentences.zh: 光以百餘人戍馬蘭山北，賊圍之百餘日。

translations.literal: Guang with more than one hundred men garrisoned north of Malan Mountain; bandits surrounded them more than one hundred days.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guang held Malan Mountain north with a hundred men for over a hundred days under siege.

sentences.zh: 光撫厲將士，屢出奇兵擊賊，破之。

translations.literal: Guang comforted and urged officers and soldiers; repeatedly deployed strange troops to strike bandits and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: He rallied his tiny garrison and repeatedly sortied to beat the besiegers.

sentences.zh: 光以兵少路遠，自分敗沒。

translations.literal: Guang because troops were few and roads distant himself judged defeat and destruction.
translations.idiomatic: He assumed doom—too few men and supply lines too long.

sentences.zh: 會梁王肜遣司馬索靖將兵迎光，舉軍悲泣，遂還長安。

translations.literal: When Prince Liang Xiong dispatched Major Suo Jing leading troops to welcome Guang, the whole army wept sadly; thereupon returned to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Then Prince Liang Sima Xiong sent Suo Jing to lift the siege; the defenders wept with relief and marched back to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 肜表光「處絕圍之地，有耿恭之忠，宜加甄賞，以明獎勸」。

translations.literal: Xiong memorialized Guang "dwelling in terrain of severed siege, having Geng Gong's loyalty—it is fitting to add selective reward to clarify encouragement."
translations.idiomatic: Sima Xiong reported Zhang Guang's loyalty rivaled Geng Gong's stand at Shule.

sentences.zh: 於是擢授新平太守，加鼓吹。

translations.literal: Thereupon promoted appointed Administrator of Xinping and granted drum band.
translations.idiomatic: The court named him Xinping prefect with an honorary band.

sentences.zh: 屬雍州刺史劉沈被密詔討河間王顒，光起兵助沈。

translations.literal: Belonging to Yong Province Inspector Liu Shen receiving secret edict to attack Prince Hejian Yong; Guang raised troops to aid Shen.
translations.idiomatic: When Yong Inspector Liu Shen moved secretly against Prince Hejian Sima Yong, Zhang Guang mobilized to support Shen.

sentences.zh: 沈時委任秦州刺史皇甫重，重自以關西大族，心每輕光，謀多不用。

translations.literal: At the time Shen entrusted Qin Province Inspector Huangfu Chong; Chong himself regarded his western-pass great clan and always slighted Guang in heart; stratagems often were not used.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shen had delegated Inspector Huangfu Chong of Qinzhou, who looked down on Zhang Guang as a mere soldier and ignored his counsel.

sentences.zh: 及二州軍潰，為顒所擒，顒謂光曰：「前起兵欲作何策？

translations.literal: When the two provinces' armies collapsed, he was captured by Yong; Yong said to Guang: "Earlier raising troops, what stratagem did you intend?"
translations.idiomatic: When both armies broke, Sima Yong seized Zhang Guang and demanded his motive for joining Liu Shen.

sentences.zh: 」光正色答曰：「但劉雍州不用鄙計，故令大王得有今日也。

translations.literal: " Guang with stern color replied: "Only because Liu Yongzhou did not employ my humble plan—therefore he let the Great King attain today."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guang answered coldly that Liu Shen had ignored his advice and thus handed Sima Yong victory.

sentences.zh: 」顒壯之，引與歡宴彌日，表為右衛司馬。

translations.literal: " Yong thought him stalwart; led him to joyous banquet a full day; memorialized him as Right Guards Major of the Horse.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yong admired his nerve, feasted him for days, and recommended him as major on the right guard.

sentences.zh: 陳敏作亂，除光順陽太守，加陵江將軍，率步騎五千詣荊州討之。

translations.literal: Chen Min made rebellion; Guang was appointed Administrator of Shunyang, added General Who Crosses the Jiang, leading infantry and cavalry five thousand to proceed to Jing Province to strike him.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Min revolted, Zhang Guang became prefect of Shunyang and General Who Crosses the Jiang with five thousand horse and foot against him.

sentences.zh: 刺史劉弘雅敬重光，稱為南楚之秀。

translations.literal: Inspector Liu Hong elegantly respected Guang and called him the finest talent of southern Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector Liu Hong esteemed him as the leading talent of southern Chu.

sentences.zh: 時江夏太守陶侃與敏大將錢端相距於長岐，將戰，襄陽太守皮初為步軍，使光設伏以待之，武陵太守苗光為水軍，藏舟艦于沔水。

translations.literal: At the time Jiangxia Administrator Tao Kan and Chen Min's great general Qian Duan opposed each other at Changqi; about to battle, Xiangyang Administrator Pi Chu was infantry; he made Guang lay ambush to await them; Wuling Administrator Miao Guang was water army, hiding boats on the Han River.
translations.idiomatic: As Tao Kan faced Qian Duan at Changqi, Pi Chu led the foot soldiers while Zhang Guang ambushed and Miao Guang hid warships on the Han.

sentences.zh: 皮初等與賊交戰，光發伏兵應之，水陸同奮，賊眾大敗。

translations.literal: Pi Chu and others engaged bandits in battle; Guang raised ambush troops to respond; water and land together exerted; the bandit multitude was greatly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Pi Chu engaged the enemy while Zhang Guang sprang the trap; land and water struck together and shattered Chen Min's army.

sentences.zh: 弘表光有殊勳，遷材官將軍，梁州刺史。

translations.literal: Hong memorialized Guang had extraordinary merit; promoted Material Works General, Inspector of Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hong cited his exceptional merit and promoted him to Material Works general and Liangzhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 先是，秦州人鄧定等二千餘家，饑餓流入漢中，保于成固，漸為抄盜，梁州刺史張殷遣巴西太守張燕討之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Qin Province men Deng Ding and others more than two thousand households, starving and hungry, flowed into Hanzhong and protected themselves at Chenggu; gradually they became raiding bandits; Liang Province Inspector Zhang Yin dispatched Ba Administrator Zhang Yan to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier more than two thousand Qinzhou households led by Deng Ding, starving, had fled into Hanzhong and fortified Chenggu until they turned to pillage; Inspector Zhang Yin sent Ba prefect Zhang Yan against them.

sentences.zh: 定窘急，偽乞降于燕，並饋燕金銀，燕喜，為之緩師。

translations.literal: Ding was pressed hard and falsely begged surrender to Yan and together gifted Yan gold and silver; Yan was pleased and for him slackened the army.
translations.idiomatic: Besieged, Deng Ding feigned surrender to Zhang Yan and bribed him with gold until Yan relaxed the siege.

sentences.zh: 定密結李雄，雄遣眾救定，燕退，定遂進逼漢中。

translations.literal: Ding secretly allied Li Xiong; Xiong dispatched a multitude to rescue Ding; Yan withdrew; Ding thereupon advanced pressing Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Ding secretly allied Li Xiong, whose reinforcements drove Zhang Yan back; Deng then pressed toward Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 太守杜正沖東奔魏興，殷亦棄官而遁。

translations.literal: Administrator Du Zhengchong fled east to Weixing; Yin also abandoned office and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Du Zhengchong fled east to Weixing while Zhang Yin abandoned his post.

sentences.zh: 光不得赴州，止于魏興，乃結諸郡守共謀進取。

translations.literal: Guang could not proceed to province; halted at Weixing; thereupon allied various prefects jointly plotting advance and seizure.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to reach his provincial seat, Zhang Guang halted at Weixing and rallied prefects for a counterattack.

sentences.zh: 燕唱言曰：「漢中荒敗，迫近大賊，克復之事，當俟英雄。

translations.literal: Yan proclaimed saying: "Hanzhong is waste and defeated; pressed near great bandits; restoration matters ought to await heroes."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yan declared Hanzhong ruined and too close to rebel forces—recovery must wait on greater heroes.

sentences.zh: 」正沖曰：「張燕受賊金銀，不時進討，阻兵緩寇，致喪漢中，實燕之罪也。

translations.literal: " Zhengchong said: "Zhang Yan received bandit gold and silver; did not timely advance and strike; blocked troops and slackened bandits—thereby losing Hanzhong; truly it is Yan's crime."
translations.idiomatic: Du Zhengchong answered that Zhang Yan had taken bribes, stalled, and lost Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 」光於是發怒，呵燕令出，斬之以徇。

translations.literal: " Guang thereupon grew angry, shouted at Yan ordering him out, executed him to display.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guang, enraged, expelled Zhang Yan and executed him as a warning.

sentences.zh: 綏撫荒殘，百姓悅服。

translations.literal: He comforted and soothed waste and remnant; the hundred surnames pleased and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: He pacified the ruined region and won popular submission.

sentences.zh: 光於是卻鎮漢中。

translations.literal: Guang thereupon withdrew to garrison Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: He then moved his headquarters back into Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 時逆賊王如餘黨李運、楊武等，自襄陽將三千餘家入漢中，光遣參軍晉邈率眾于黃金距之。

translations.literal: At the time remnant bandit Wang Ru's leftover party Li Yun, Yang Wu and others, from Xiangyang led more than three thousand households into Hanzhong; Guang dispatched adjutant Jin Miao leading troops at Huangjin to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ru's followers Li Yun and Yang Wu led three thousand households from Xiangyang into Hanzhong; Zhang Guang sent adjutant Jin Miao to block them at Huangjin.

sentences.zh: 邈受運重賂，勸光納運。

translations.literal: Miao received Yun's heavy bribe and urged Guang to admit Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Miao took Li Yun's bribes and urged Zhang Guang to shelter him.

sentences.zh: 光從邈言，使居成固。

translations.literal: Guang followed Miao's words and made them dwell at Chenggu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guang listened and quartered them at Chenggu.

sentences.zh: 既而邈以運多珍貨，又欲奪之，復言於光曰：「運之徒屬不事佃農，但營器杖，意在難測，可掩而取之。

translations.literal: Afterward Miao because Yun had many precious goods also wished to seize them; again spoke to Guang saying: "Yun's followers do not serve in farming but only craft weapons—intent is hard to fathom—one can surprise and take them."
translations.idiomatic: Then Jin Miao coveted their treasure and told Zhang Guang the refugees made arms instead of farming—their loyalty was suspect and they should be seized.

sentences.zh: 」光又信焉。

translations.literal: " Guang again believed him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guang believed him again.

sentences.zh: 遣邈眾討運，不克。

translations.literal: He dispatched Miao's multitude to attack Yun and did not conquer.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Jin Miao against Li Yun but failed.

sentences.zh: 光乞師于氐王楊茂搜，茂搜遣子難敵助之。

translations.literal: Guang begged troops from Di king Yang Maosou; Maosou dispatched son Nandi to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guang borrowed troops from Di king Yang Maosou, who sent his son Yang Nandi.

sentences.zh: 難敵求貨於光，光不與。

translations.literal: Nandi sought goods from Guang; Guang did not give.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Nandi demanded payment; Zhang Guang refused.

sentences.zh: 楊武乃厚賂難敵，謂之曰「流人寶物悉在光處，今伐我，不如伐光。

translations.literal: Yang Wu then richly bribed Nandi, saying to him "Refugees' treasures all are at Guang's place; now attacking me is not as good as attacking Guang."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Wu bribed Yang Nandi, arguing Zhang Guang hoarded the refugees' loot—strike him instead.

sentences.zh: 」難敵大喜，聲言助光，內與運同，光弗之知也，遣息援率眾助邈。

translations.literal: " Nandi greatly rejoiced; proclaimed wording aiding Guang; inwardly was together with Yun; Guang did not know it; dispatched son Yuan leading troops to assist Miao.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Nandi publicly sided with Zhang Guang while secretly joining Li Yun; Zhang Guang, unaware, sent his son Zhang Yuan to reinforce Jin Miao.

sentences.zh: 運與難敵夾攻邈等，援為流矢所中死，賊遂大盛。

translations.literal: Yun and Nandi jointly attacked Miao and others; Yuan was hit by a stray arrow and died; bandits thereupon greatly flourished.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yun and Yang Nandi crushed Jin Miao; Zhang Yuan fell to a stray shaft and the rebels swelled.

sentences.zh: 光嬰城固守，自夏迄冬，憤激成疾。

translations.literal: Guang rounded the city firmly defending; from summer reaching winter indignation swelled into illness.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guang held the walls from summer through winter until wrath turned to sickness.

sentences.zh: 佐吏及百姓咸勸光退據魏興，光按劍曰：「吾受國厚恩，不能翦除寇賊，今得自死，便如登仙，何得退還也！

translations.literal: Adjutants and commoners all urged Guang to withdraw and occupy Weixing; Guang grasped his sword saying: "I received the state's thick grace; cannot extirpate bandits and bandits; now getting to die myself is like ascending immortals—how could I withdraw and return!"
translations.idiomatic: Staff and citizens begged him to fall back to Weixing, but he gripped his sword and swore he would rather die defending Hanzhong than retreat.

sentences.zh: 」聲絕而卒，時年五十五。

translations.literal: " Voice broke and he died; at the time age fifty-five.
translations.idiomatic: His voice failed as he died at fifty-five.

sentences.zh: 百姓悲泣，遠近傷惜之。

translations.literal: The hundred surnames wept sadly; far and near wounded and pitied him.
translations.idiomatic: People across the region mourned him.

sentences.zh: 有二子炅、邁。

translations.literal: He had two sons Jiong and Mai.
translations.idiomatic: He left sons Zhang Jiong and Zhang Mai.

sentences.zh: 炅少辟太宰掾。

translations.literal: Jiong in youth was summoned Grand Marshal aide.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jiong served young as aide to the Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 邁多才略，有父風。

translations.literal: Mai had much talent and stratagem; had father's manner.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Mai inherited his father's tactical brilliance.

sentences.zh: 州人推邁權領州事，與賊戰沒。

translations.literal: Provincials pushed Mai to interim lead provincial affairs; battling bandits he perished in the ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Locals made Zhang Mai interim inspector until he fell fighting rebels.

sentences.zh: 別駕範曠及督護王喬奉光妻息，率其遺眾，還據魏興。

translations.literal: Assistant Administrator Fan Kuang and inspector Wang Qiao attended Guang's wife and children, leading his remnant host, returning to occupy Weixing.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Kuang and Wang Qiao escorted Zhang Guang's family and survivors back to Weixing.

sentences.zh: 其後義陽太守任愔為梁州，光妻子歸本郡。

translations.literal: Later Yiyang Administrator Ren Yin became Liang Province; Guang's wife and children returned to home commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Later Ren Yin of Yiyang became Liangzhou inspector and Zhang Guang's kin returned home.

sentences.zh: 南平太守應詹白都督王敦，稱「光在梁州能興微繼絕，威振巴漢。

translations.literal: Nanping Administrator Ying Zhan informed supervisor Wang Dun, stating "Guang at Liang Province was able to revive what was slight and continue what was cut off; awe shook Ba and Han."
translations.idiomatic: Ying Zhan of Nanping wrote Wang Dun that Zhang Guang had restored ruined Liangzhou and awed Ba and Han.

sentences.zh: 值中原傾覆，征鎮失守，外無救助，內闕資儲，以寡敵眾，經年抗禦，厲節不撓，宜應追論顯贈，以慰存亡」。

translations.literal: " Encountering the Central Plain's overturning, expedition garrisons lost guard; outside none aided rescue; inside lacked provisions storage—using few to oppose many, through years resisting defense; stern integrity unyielding—it is fitting to pursue deliberation and prominent posthumous grant to console surviving and dead."
translations.idiomatic: With no aid amid collapse, Zhang Guang had held out with scant supplies—he deserved posthumous honors.

sentences.zh: 敦不能從。

translations.literal: Dun could not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun refused.

sentences.zh: 趙誘

translations.literal: Zhao You — biography heading.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao You.

sentences.zh: 趙誘，字元孫，淮南人也。

translations.literal: Zhao You, courtesy name Yuansun, was a man of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao You, courtesy Yuansun, came from Huainan.

sentences.zh: 世以將顯。

translations.literal: For generations they displayed as generals.
translations.idiomatic: His family rose through military service.

sentences.zh: 州辟主簿。

translations.literal: The province summoned him chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: The province appointed him chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 值刺史郗隆被齊王冏檄，使起兵討趙王倫，隆欲承檄舉義，而諸子侄並在洛陽；

translations.literal: When Inspector Xi Long received Prince Qi's proclamation ordering him to raise troops to attack Prince Zhao Lun, Long wished to accept the proclamation and raise righteous arms, but all sons and nephews were in Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Inspector Xi Long received Sima Jiong's call to march against Sima Lun, he wanted to comply but his kin remained hostage in Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 欲坐觀成敗，恐為冏所討，進退有疑，會群吏計議。

translations.literal: He wished to sit and watch success or defeat; feared being attacked by Jiong; advance and retreat had doubt; he convened group clerks to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: He hesitated between joining Sima Jiong and staying neutral for fear of reprisal.

sentences.zh: 誘說隆曰：「趙王篡逆，海內所病。

translations.literal: You persuaded Long saying: "Prince Zhao usurps rebellion—within the seas all find it sickening."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao You urged Xi Long that Sima Lun's usurpation disgusted the realm.

sentences.zh: 今義兵飆起，其敗必矣。

translations.literal: " Now righteous troops whirl rising—their defeat is certain."
translations.idiomatic: "The loyal armies will crush him."

sentences.zh: 今為明使君計，莫若自將精兵，徑赴許昌，上策也。

translations.literal: " Now for enlightened envoy lord's planning, nothing equals personally leading elite troops, proceeding straight to Xuchang—upper stratagem."
translations.idiomatic: Best choice: lead elite troops straight to Xuchang.

sentences.zh: 不然，且可留後，遣猛將將兵會盟，亦中策也。

translations.literal: " Otherwise, for the moment stay behind, dispatch fierce generals leading troops to covenant alliance—also middle stratagem."
translations.idiomatic: Middle course: stay put but send a strong column to join the league.

sentences.zh: 若遣小軍隨形助勝。

translations.literal: " If dispatching small army following form aiding victory."
translations.idiomatic: Worst: dispatch only token aid.

sentences.zh: 下策耳。

translations.literal: Lower stratagem only.
translations.idiomatic: That is the lowest option.

sentences.zh: 」隆曰：「我受二帝恩，無所偏助，正欲保州而已。

translations.literal: " Long said: "I received two Emperors' grace; I have no partial aid—I only wish to protect the province."
translations.idiomatic: Xi Long refused to take sides, claiming he owed both emperors and wanted only to guard his province.

sentences.zh: 」誘與治中留寶、主簿張褒等諫隆：「若無所助，變難將生，州亦不可保也。

translations.literal: " You together with administration aide Liu Bao, chief clerk Zhang Bao and others remonstrated Long: "If there is no aid whatsoever, change and disaster will arise—the province also cannot be preserved."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao You, Liu Bao, and Zhang Bao warned that neutrality would invite disaster.

sentences.zh: 」隆猶豫不決，遂為其下所害。

translations.literal: " Long hesitated undecided; thereupon was harmed by his subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Long vacillated until his own troops killed him.

sentences.zh: 誘還家，杜門不出。

translations.literal: You returned home; blocked gate and did not go out.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao You retired home and shut his gates.

sentences.zh: 左將軍王敦以為參軍，加廣武將軍，與甘卓、周訪共討華軼，破之。

translations.literal: Left General Wang Dun employed him as staff adviser, added General Who Displays Martial Might; together with Gan Zhuo and Zhou Fang jointly attacked Hua Yi and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun made him adviser and General Who Displays Martial Might; with Gan Zhuo and Zhou Fang he crushed Hua Yi.

sentences.zh: 又擊杜弢於西湘，太興初，復與卓攻弢，滅之。

translations.literal: Again struck Du Tao at western Xiang; early in Taixing again with Zhuo attacked Tao and extinguished him.
translations.idiomatic: He fought Du Tao in western Xiang and, early in Taixing, helped Gan Zhuo destroy him.

sentences.zh: 累功賜爵平阿縣侯，代陶侃為武昌太守。

translations.literal: By accumulated merit granted noble rank Baron of Ping'e; replaced Tao Kan as Administrator of Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Merit won him the Ping'e barony and Wuchang prefecture after Tao Kan.

sentences.zh: 時杜曾迎第五猗於荊州作亂，敦遣誘與襄陽太守朱軌共距之。

translations.literal: At the time Du Zeng welcomed Fifth Yi from Jing Province to make rebellion; Dun dispatched You together with Xiangyang Administrator Zhu Gui jointly to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: When Du Zeng raised Fifth Yi in Jingzhou, Wang Dun sent Zhao You and Zhu Gui of Xiangyang to oppose them.

sentences.zh: 猗既愍帝所遣，加有時望，為荊楚所歸。

translations.literal: Yi was both whom Emperor Min dispatched and moreover had timely reputation—Jing and Chu attached to him.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth Yi bore Emperor Min's commission and enjoyed prestige—Jingzhou rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 誘等苦戰皆沒，敦甚悼惜之，表贈征虜將軍、秦州刺史，諡曰敬。

translations.literal: You and others bitterly fought all perished; Dun greatly mourned and pitied him; memorialized posthumous award General Who Conquers the Caitiffs, Inspector of Qin Province; posthumous title Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao You and Zhu Gui died fighting; Wang Dun mourned them and posthumously named Zhao You General Who Conquers the Caitiffs and Qinzhou inspector with epithet Jing.

sentences.zh: 子龔，與誘俱死。

translations.literal: Son Gong together with You both died.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhao Gong fell beside him.

sentences.zh: 元帝為晉王，下令贈新昌太守。

translations.literal: Prince Yuan as Prince of Jin issued order posthumously investing Xinchang Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yuan posthumously named him Xinchang prefect.

sentences.zh: 龔弟胤，字伯舒。

translations.literal: Gong's younger brother Yin, courtesy name Boshi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Gong's brother Yin, courtesy Boshi.

sentences.zh: 王敦使周訪擊杜曾，胤請從行。

translations.literal: Wang Dun sent Zhou Fang strike Du Zeng; Yin requested to follow the march.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Dun ordered Zhou Fang against Du Zeng, Zhao Yin volunteered.

sentences.zh: 訪憚曾之強，欲先以胤餌曾，使其眾疲而後擊之。

translations.literal: Fang dreaded Zeng's strength; wished first to use Yin as bait to Zeng, making his multitude weary afterward striking them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Fang feared Du Zeng and meant to use Zhao Yin as bait to tire him.

sentences.zh: 胤多梟首級。

translations.literal: Yin many times beheaded heads.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yin nonetheless piled up heads.

sentences.zh: 王導引為從事中郎。

translations.literal: Wang Dao drew him as attendant clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao recruited him as attendant clerk.

sentences.zh: 南頓王宗反，胤殺宗。

translations.literal: Prince Nandun Zong rebelled; Yin killed Zong.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Sima Zong of Nandun rebelled, Zhao Yin executed him.

sentences.zh: 於是王導、庾亮並倚仗之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Wang Dao and Yu Liang both relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao and Yu Liang both relied on him thereafter.

sentences.zh: 轉冠軍將軍，遷西豫州刺史，卒于官。

translations.literal: Transferred General Who Champions the Army; promoted Western Yu Province Inspector; died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to General Who Champions the Army and western Yu Province inspector before dying in office.

sentences.zh: 史評

translations.literal: Historians' appraisal heading.
translations.idiomatic: Historians' appraisal.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：忠為令德，貞曰事君，徇國家而竭身，曆夷險而一節。

translations.literal: The historians say: Loyalty is excellent virtue; steadfastness is called serving lord; Following state and exhausting body; traversing peril and smooth with one integrity.
translations.idiomatic: The historians praise loyalty as supreme virtue and steadfast service through danger and calm alike.

sentences.zh: 羅憲、滕修，濯纓入仕，指巴東而受脤，出嶺嶠而揚麾。

translations.literal: Luo Xian, Teng Xiu—washing tassels entering office—pointed to Badong when receiving sacrificial meat; exited mountain ranges and waved banners.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Xian and Teng Xiu entered office as honest officials, commanded Badong, and led armies beyond the southern ranges.

sentences.zh: 屬鼎命淪胥，本朝失守，郕巴丘而流涕，集都亭而大臨。

translations.literal: When dynastic mandate sank away and this court lost guard, they tarried at Baqiu weeping tears; gathered at metropolitan pavilion for great mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When dynasties fell they mourned at Baqiu and the metropolitan pavilion like loyal mourners of a fallen sovereign.

sentences.zh: 古之忠烈，罕輩子茲！

translations.literal: Ancient loyalty and fierce devotion—rarely are peers found here!
translations.idiomatic: Few ancient exemplars of loyalty match them.

sentences.zh: 孝興之智勇，玄威之武藝，滅醜虜於河西，制凶酋於硜北，審楊欣之必敗，譏楊駿之速禍。

translations.literal: Xiaoxing's wisdom and courage, Xuanwei's martial arts—destroyed ugly barbarians west of the River, restrained fierce chiefs north of Jing; discerned Yang Xin's certain defeat, ridiculed Yang Jun's hastened disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Long's courage and Hu Fen's arms crushed foes west of the river and north of Jing; Long foresaw Yang Xin's fall and Fen mocked Yang Jun's folly.

sentences.zh: 陶璜、吾彥，逸足齊驅，毛炅屈其深謀，陸抗奇其茂略。

translations.literal: Tao Huang and Wu Yan—swift horses raced together—Mao Jiong bent before their deep stratagem; Lu Kang marveled at their lush planning.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Huang and Wu Yan rivaled swift steeds; Mao Jiong bowed to Huang's schemes and Lu Kang noted Wu Yan's genius.

sentences.zh: 薪楢之任，清規自遠；

translations.literal: Timber fuel's burden—clean norms from afar;
translations.idiomatic: Their frontier burdens bred integrity from afar.

sentences.zh: 鼙鼓之臣，厥聲彌劭。

translations.literal: Drum-and-war ministers—their fame grows ever brighter.
translations.idiomatic: These drum-table generals grew ever more renowned.

sentences.zh: 景武，南楚秀士；

translations.literal: Jingwu—southern Chu's fine scholar;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guang was southern Chu's brilliant commander.

sentences.zh: 元孫，累葉將門，赴死喻於登仙。

translations.literal: Yuansun—many generations general's gate—rushing death compared to ascending immortals.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao You's warrior house chose death as gladly as immortals.

sentences.zh: 效誠陳於上策，竟而俱斃，貞則斯存。

translations.literal: Displaying loyalty presenting upper stratagem—yet together perished—steadfast purpose thus endures.
translations.idiomatic: They offered loyal counsel yet died together—yet integrity survives them.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：憲居玉疊，才博流譽。

translations.literal: Praise says: Xian dwelt on Jade Stack—talent broad, fame flowing.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium sings Luo Xian's fame atop the Jade Walls.

sentences.zh: 修赴石門，惠政攸著。

translations.literal: Xiu hastened to Stone Gate—kind governance stood manifest.
translations.idiomatic: Teng Xiu's kindness showed at Stone Gate.

sentences.zh: 孝興、玄威，操履無違。

translations.literal: Xiaoxing and Xuanwei—conduct and treading without violation.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Long and Hu Fen kept unstained conduct.

sentences.zh: 愚墳畢禮，楊門致譏。

translations.literal: Yu tomb finished rites—the Yang gate incurred ridicule.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Fen's tomb honors Yang Jun yet drew mockery.

sentences.zh: 璜謀超絕，彥材雄傑。

translations.literal: Huang's stratagem surpassed others; Yan's talent heroic and outstanding.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Huang's designs were supreme; Wu Yan towered among heroes.

sentences.zh: 潛師襲董，觀兵歎薛。

translations.literal: Hidden troops struck Dong; viewing troops sighed at Xue.
translations.idiomatic: Huang surprised Dong Yuan and Wu Yan studied Xue Xu.

sentences.zh: 惟趙與張，神略多方。

translations.literal: Only Zhao together with Zhang—divine stratagem many-sided.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao You and Zhang Guang wielded versatile genius.

sentences.zh: 作尉北地，立功西湘。

translations.literal: Serving as commandant north of the earth—establishing merit western Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: They commanded the northern march and won laurels on western Xiang.
